</table>
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}_{i}\perp\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐮</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⟂</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}_{i}\perp\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> is a decoy output direction and <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta,s&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta,s&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> are scalar gains. For SwiGLU in replace mode, writing <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{\ell}\mathrel{\triangleq}\langle\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell},\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\ell}\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{\ell}\mathrel{\triangleq}\langle\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell},\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\ell}\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> for the neuron’s refusal coordinate, its decoy contribution is</p>
<table id="S3.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{i}(\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\ell})=s\,g_{\beta}(a_{\ell})\,\mathbf{u}_{i},\qquad g_{\beta}(a)\mathrel{\triangleq}a\,\operatorname{silu}(\beta a)=\beta a^{2}\sigma(\beta a)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>β</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐮</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>β</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0.337em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>silu</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{i}(\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\ell})=s\,g_{\beta}(a_{\ell})\,\mathbf{u}_{i},\qquad g_{\beta}(a)\mathrel{\triangleq}a\,\operatorname{silu}(\beta a)=\beta a^{2}\sigma(\beta a),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> is the logistic sigmoid. The sigmoid suppresses the gate for negative refusal coordinates; for large positive coordinates, <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\beta}(a)\approx\beta a^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>β</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\beta}(a)\approx\beta a^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. This produces larger decoy shifts on prompts with positive refusal coordinates.
DDO estimates <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> via DIM on post-attention-layernorm activations <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\ell}=\mathrm{RMSNorm}(\mathbf{h}_{\ell}^{\mathrm{attn}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>RMSNorm</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐡</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>attn</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\ell}=\mathrm{RMSNorm}(\mathbf{h}_{\ell}^{\mathrm{attn}})</annotation></semantics></math>, the same space that <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{gate}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>gate</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{gate}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{up}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>up</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{up}}</annotation></semantics></math> read from. The decoy output through <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>down</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}</annotation></semantics></math> writes directly to the residual stream.
We parameterize <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\mathbf{u}_{i}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>𝐮</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\mathbf{u}_{i}\}</annotation></semantics></math> as unit vectors constrained to remain orthogonal to <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>. We initialize by sampling <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}_{i}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\mathbf{I})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐈</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}_{i}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\mathbf{I})</annotation></semantics></math>, projecting onto <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}^{\perp}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⟂</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}^{\perp}</annotation></semantics></math>, and orthonormalizing, then gradient-optimize <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\mathbf{u}_{i}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>𝐮</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\mathbf{u}_{i}\}</annotation></semantics></math> to maximize estimator confusion.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Multiple decoy readers.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">With a shared reader and gate, all edited neurons respond through the same scalar <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\beta}(a_{\ell})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>β</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\beta}(a_{\ell})</annotation></semantics></math>. To obtain more varied responses, DDO (rank <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>) partitions the <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> edited neurons into <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> groups. Group <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> uses a perturbed reader</p>
<table id="S3.Ex3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathbf{q}_{\ell,g}=\frac{\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}+\gamma\mathbf{z}_{\ell,g}}{\|\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}+\gamma\mathbf{z}_{\ell,g}\|_{2}},\qquad\mathbf{z}_{\ell,g}\perp\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell},\qquad g=1,\ldots,K," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐪</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mfrac><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mi>𝐳</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></msub><mo>⟂</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><msub><mrow></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{q}_{\ell,g}=\frac{\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}+\gamma\mathbf{z}_{\ell,g}}{\|\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}+\gamma\mathbf{z}_{\ell,g}\|_{2}},\qquad\mathbf{z}_{\ell,g}\perp\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell},\qquad g=1,\ldots,K,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{z}_{\ell,g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{z}_{\ell,g}</annotation></semantics></math> is random and <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> controls reader diversity. Its neurons use <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{q}_{\ell,g}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐪</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{q}_{\ell,g}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math> in the up-projection and <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{g}\mathbf{q}_{\ell,g}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐪</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{g}\mathbf{q}_{\ell,g}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math> in the gate-projection. Distinct readers allow decoy responses to vary differently across prompts; the spectral analysis below explains the resulting tradeoff between strength and rank.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">DDO gradient optimization.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">DDO optimizes decoy directions <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\mathbf{u}_{i}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>𝐮</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\mathbf{u}_{i}\}</annotation></semantics></math> via gradient descent through the defended model, while all base-model weights remain frozen. Scalar gains <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\beta,s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\beta,s)</annotation></semantics></math> are treated as hyperparameters and tuned via Bayesian hyperparameter search (Optuna; Appendix <a href="#A6.SS6" title="F.6 Per-Model DDO Best Configs ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.6</span></a>). The optimization minimizes a composite loss over 128 harmful and 128 safe probes:</p>
<table id="S3.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}=\lambda_{\text{ref}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{refuse}}+\lambda_{\text{ret}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{retain}}+\lambda_{\text{conf}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{confusion}}+\lambda_{\text{rs}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{refusal-score}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>ref</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>refuse</mtext></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>ret</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>retain</mtext></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>conf</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>confusion</mtext></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>rs</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>refusal-score</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}=\lambda_{\text{ref}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{refuse}}+\lambda_{\text{ret}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{retain}}+\lambda_{\text{conf}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{confusion}}+\lambda_{\text{rs}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{refusal-score}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">with <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\text{ref}}{=}\lambda_{\text{ret}}{=}\lambda_{\text{rs}}{=}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>ref</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>ret</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>rs</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\text{ref}}{=}\lambda_{\text{ret}}{=}\lambda_{\text{rs}}{=}1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\text{conf}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>conf</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\text{conf}}</annotation></semantics></math> tuned per model (Table <a href="#A6.T13" title="Table 13 ‣ F.6 Per-Model DDO Best Configs ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>), where (i) <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{refuse}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>refuse</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{refuse}}</annotation></semantics></math> (<em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">refusal preservation</em>) is cross-entropy on harmful prompts toward a refusal continuation; (ii) <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{retain}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>retain</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{retain}}</annotation></semantics></math> (<em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">benign retention</em>) is KL divergence to the frozen base model on safe prompts; (iii) <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{confusion}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>confusion</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{confusion}}</annotation></semantics></math> (<em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">estimator confusion</em>) is a differentiable self-RFA simulator that re-estimates DIM on the current defended weights, applies ablation, and minimizes KL divergence between defended and ablated output logits, pushing the estimated DIM direction toward the decoy subspace; and (iv) <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{refusal-score}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>refusal-score</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{refusal-score}}</annotation></semantics></math> (<em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">first-token anchoring</em>) is a first-token logit margin between refusal-prefixed tokens ({<span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">I</span>, <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Sorry</span>, <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">cannot</span>}) and compliance-prefixed tokens ({<span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Sure</span>, <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Here</span>}). Without this term, the model can satisfy sequence-level losses by emitting a compliance token followed by a mid-sentence pivot to refusal (“Sure, I’d be happy to…actually I cannot”), a degenerate solution that does not produce genuine refusal at generation time (Appendix <a href="#A4.SS1" title="D.1 First-Token Collapse ‣ Appendix D Additional Method Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.1</span></a>).
After each gradient step, we re-project each <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐮</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> onto <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}^{\perp}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⟂</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}^{\perp}</annotation></semantics></math>, Gram-Schmidt orthogonalize the decoy directions within each layer, and renormalize. For one hyperparameter configuration, including direction estimation, optimization, and weight surgery, DDO takes <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\sim}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\sim}</annotation></semantics></math>2 minutes per optimization run on a single A100 GPU.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Compile mode.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">DDO parameters are compiled into model weights using either <em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">replace</em> mode (overwriting neuron weights for a stronger decoy signal) or <em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">additive</em> mode (superposing the decoy on original weights, preserving the neuron’s original computation). The preferred mode is model-specific: replace is preferred on Yi <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>]</cite>, Llama-3, and GLM-4 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a>]</cite>; additive on Gemma-2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">29</a>]</cite>, Qwen3 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">30</a>]</cite>, and Mistral <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">31</a>]</cite> (Appendix <a href="#A6.SS4" title="F.4 Compile Mode Selection Details ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.4</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Layer placement.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">DDO decoys must be placed at or before the model’s <em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">causal refusal zone</em>—the layers whose ablation causally reduces refusal (Appendix <a href="#A6.SS3" title="F.3 Per-Model Causal Refusal Zones ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.3</span></a>). We say refusal is <em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">localized</em> when ablating any single layer in this zone causes near-complete refusal loss, and <em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">distributed</em> when refusal is redundant across many layers so that ablating any one only partially reduces it. Placing decoys <em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">inside</em> the causal zone can disrupt baseline refusal and increase vulnerability under attack on models with localized refusal. <em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.5" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Upstream</em> placement preserves refusal while still contaminating the attacker’s estimator. On models with distributed or sparse refusal patterns (Yi, Llama-2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">32</a>]</cite>), placement has less impact (Appendix <a href="#A6.SS5" title="F.5 Layer Placement Analysis ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.5</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Spectral analysis of contrastive ablation.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">DDO aims to make decoy signals dominate the harmful–safe contrast. We analyze this effect through the overlap between the attacker’s selected directions and the refusal subspace. The results proceed in three steps: a general overlap bound, its specialization to DDO, and a design rule for distributing decoy strength.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Fix a layer and token position, and suppress their indices. Let <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>⊆</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> be the causal refusal subspace, with orthogonal projector <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pi_{\mathcal{R}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pi_{\mathcal{R}}</annotation></semantics></math>. A contrastive attacker forms <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times N}</annotation></semantics></math> and ablates its top-<math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> left singular directions. Write</p>
<table id="S3.Ex4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pi_{k}(C)\mathrel{\triangleq}Q_{k}(C)Q_{k}(C)^{\top}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≜</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pi_{k}(C)\mathrel{\triangleq}Q_{k}(C)Q_{k}(C)^{\top},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{k}(C)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{k}(C)</annotation></semantics></math> contains those <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> singular vectors. Standard rank-1 DIM uses the single-column matrix <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C=\mathbf{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝐝</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C=\mathbf{d}</annotation></semantics></math>; a higher-rank SVD attack uses per-sample harmful–safe contrasts as columns. The overlap <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\Pi_{\mathcal{R}}\Pi_{k}(C)\|_{\mathrm{op}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>op</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\Pi_{\mathcal{R}}\Pi_{k}(C)\|_{\mathrm{op}}</annotation></semantics></math> lies in <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>: zero means the subspaces are orthogonal, and one means they share a direction. We write <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{j}(C)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{j}(C)</annotation></semantics></math> for the <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>-th largest singular value, <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.m12" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{op}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo rspace="0em">∥</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em">∥</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>op</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{op}}</annotation></semantics></math> for the matrix operator norm, and <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p2.m13" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\|\cdot\|_{F}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo rspace="0em">∥</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em">∥</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\cdot\|_{F}</annotation></semantics></math> for the Frobenius norm.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 1</span></span><span id="Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Subspace overlap bound)<span id="Thmtheorem1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For <math id="Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\leq k\leq\min(d,N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\leq k\leq\min(d,N)</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{k}(C)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{k}(C)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, the attacker’s ablation subspace satisfies</span></p>
<table id="S3.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left\|\Pi_{\mathcal{R}}\Pi_{k}(C)\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\frac{\left\|\Pi_{\mathcal{R}}C\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}}{\sigma_{k}(C)}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mo>‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>‖</mo></mrow><mi>op</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><msub><mrow><mo>‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><mo>‖</mo></mrow><mi>op</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\|\Pi_{\mathcal{R}}\Pi_{k}(C)\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\frac{\left\|\Pi_{\mathcal{R}}C\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}}{\sigma_{k}(C)}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The numerator measures the refusal signal in the contrast; the denominator is the strength of the weakest singular direction the attacker selects. A small ratio therefore implies little refusal overlap. DDO seeks to strengthen the contrast along decoy directions while preserving the underlying refusal computation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Decoy contrast decomposition.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For DDO, decompose the defended contrast into a decoy component and a remainder:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{\theta}=D_{\theta}+S_{\theta},\qquad D_{\theta}=UA_{\theta}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{\theta}=D_{\theta}+S_{\theta},\qquad D_{\theta}=UA_{\theta}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The columns of <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times m}</annotation></semantics></math> are <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> orthonormal decoy write directions. The <em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">decoy response matrix</em> <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{\theta}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{\theta}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times N}</annotation></semantics></math> records their contributions across contrast samples: <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{\theta}[i,j]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{\theta}[i,j]</annotation></semantics></math> is the coefficient of <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐮</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> in the <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>-th decoy contrast. The remainder <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> contains all other contributions. Define</p>
<table id="S3.Ex6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.3" class="ltx_p">the total residual magnitude and its refusal component, respectively.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 2</span></span><span id="Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Overlap bound under orthogonal decoys)<span id="Thmtheorem2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For the decomposition above, assume <math id="Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U^{\top}U=I_{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>U</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>U</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U^{\top}U=I_{m}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pi_{\mathcal{R}}U=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>U</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pi_{\mathcal{R}}U=0</annotation></semantics></math>. If <math id="Thmtheorem2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\leq k\leq\min(m,N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\leq k\leq\min(m,N)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="Thmtheorem2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{k}(A_{\theta})&gt;\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>ρ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{k}(A_{\theta})&gt;\rho</annotation></semantics></math>, then</span></p>
<table id="S3.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left\|\Pi_{\mathcal{R}}\Pi_{k}(C_{\theta})\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\frac{\rho_{\mathcal{R}}}{\sigma_{k}(A_{\theta})-\rho}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mo>‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>‖</mo></mrow><mi>op</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></msub><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>ρ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\|\Pi_{\mathcal{R}}\Pi_{k}(C_{\theta})\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\frac{\rho_{\mathcal{R}}}{\sigma_{k}(A_{\theta})-\rho}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The denominator is a <em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">spectral margin</em>: the <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>-th decoy mode must exceed the residual magnitude. At fixed <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{\mathcal{R}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{\mathcal{R}}</annotation></semantics></math>, a larger margin gives a smaller overlap bound. The idealized orthogonality condition puts all refusal signal in <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>; DDO approximates it by enforcing <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}_{i}\perp\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐮</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⟂</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}_{i}\perp\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For an overlap tolerance <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0&lt;\varepsilon&lt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>ε</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0&lt;\varepsilon&lt;1</annotation></semantics></math>, define the <em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">effective decoy rank</em></p>
<table id="S3.Ex7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\mathrm{eff}}(\varepsilon)\mathrel{\triangleq}\#\left\{1\leq j\leq\min(m,N):\sigma_{j}(A_{\theta})&gt;\rho+\frac{\rho_{\mathcal{R}}}{\varepsilon}\right\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>eff</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ε</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mi>#</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi><mo rspace="0.278em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></msub><mi>ε</mi></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\mathrm{eff}}(\varepsilon)\mathrel{\triangleq}\#\left\{1\leq j\leq\min(m,N):\sigma_{j}(A_{\theta})&gt;\rho+\frac{\rho_{\mathcal{R}}}{\varepsilon}\right\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p3.2" class="ltx_p">For a fixed contrast matrix, this counts the decoy modes strong enough to keep overlap at most <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ε</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon</annotation></semantics></math>: Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 2 (Overlap bound under orthogonal decoys). ‣ Decoy contrast decomposition. ‣ 3 Method: Decoy Direction Optimization (DDO) ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> applies to every <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\leq k\leq r_{\mathrm{eff}}(\varepsilon)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>eff</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ε</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\leq k\leq r_{\mathrm{eff}}(\varepsilon)</annotation></semantics></math>. Adaptive RFA changes the contrast after each phase, so <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\mathrm{eff}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>eff</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\mathrm{eff}}</annotation></semantics></math> is a diagnostic for interpreting phase budgets, rather than a guarantee for iterative re-estimation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px8" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Decoy energy allocation.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Shared readers produce responses that vary together, so adding write directions alone need not create additional strong decoy modes. The diversified readers introduced above allow several modes, but a fixed energy budget limits their individual strength.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_corollary">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmtheorem3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 3</span></span><span id="Thmtheorem3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Optimal spectrum under an energy constraint)<span id="Thmtheorem3.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For <math id="Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{\theta}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{\theta}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times N}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\leq k\leq\min(m,N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\leq k\leq\min(m,N)</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="Thmtheorem3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|A_{\theta}\|_{F}\leq B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|A_{\theta}\|_{F}\leq B</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="Thmtheorem3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{k}(A_{\theta})\leq B/\sqrt{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>/</mo><msqrt><mi>k</mi></msqrt></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{k}(A_{\theta})\leq B/\sqrt{k}</annotation></semantics></math>. The bound is attained by allocating equal energy to the first <math id="Thmtheorem3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> singular modes:</span></p>
<table id="S3.Ex8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex8.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\sigma_{1}(A_{\theta})=\cdots=\sigma_{k}(A_{\theta})=\frac{B}{\sqrt{k}},\qquad\sigma_{j}(A_{\theta})=0\quad(j&gt;k)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0.1389em">⋯</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em">=</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>B</mi><msqrt><mi>k</mi></msqrt></mfrac><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{1}(A_{\theta})=\cdots=\sigma_{k}(A_{\theta})=\frac{B}{\sqrt{k}},\qquad\sigma_{j}(A_{\theta})=0\quad(j&gt;k).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px8.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px8.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For rank-1 protection, concentrating energy gives the strongest possible leading decoy mode. Protecting against larger ranks requires sharing that energy across more modes, each of which is weaker. This strength–rank tradeoff motivates DDO’s <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px8.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> reader groups. Proofs are in Appendix <a href="#A5.SS1" title="E.1 Proofs of the Overlap and Spectral Bounds ‣ Appendix E Theoretical Proofs and Formalizations ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.1</span></a>; Appendix <a href="#A5.SS2" title="E.2 Stackelberg Formulation ‣ Appendix E Theoretical Proofs and Formalizations ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.2</span></a> discusses the broader attacker–defender interaction.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px9" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Orthogonal debiasing (utility repair).</h4>

<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">DDO can introduce mild over-refusal <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">33</a>]</cite> on some models. We repair this with <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px9.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">orthogonal debiasing</span>: projecting out an over-refusal direction <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{v}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐯</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{v}}</annotation></semantics></math> estimated from benign prompts the model incorrectly refuses <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>, <a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">35</a>]</cite>. For matrices where the residual stream is the <em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px9.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">input</em> dimension (<math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px9.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{gate}},\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{up}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>gate</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>up</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{gate}},\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{up}}</annotation></semantics></math>): <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px9.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}^{\prime}=\mathbf{W}-(\mathbf{W}\hat{\mathbf{v}})\hat{\mathbf{v}}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝐖</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐯</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐯</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}^{\prime}=\mathbf{W}-(\mathbf{W}\hat{\mathbf{v}})\hat{\mathbf{v}}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>. For matrices where the residual stream is the <em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px9.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">output</em> dimension (<math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px9.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{o},\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>down</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{o},\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}</annotation></semantics></math>): <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px9.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}^{\prime}=\mathbf{W}-\hat{\mathbf{v}}(\hat{\mathbf{v}}^{\top}\mathbf{W})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐯</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐯</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐖</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}^{\prime}=\mathbf{W}-\hat{\mathbf{v}}(\hat{\mathbf{v}}^{\top}\mathbf{W})</annotation></semantics></math>. We apply this to <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px9.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{emb}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>emb</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{emb}}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px9.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{o}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{o}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px9.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>down</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Experiments and Results</h2>

<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Experimental Setup</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">DDO edits are applied to model weights before deployment; the defended checkpoint incurs no architectural or runtime overhead. We compare against trained baselines under the same evaluation protocol. For all defenses, we report (i) utility and benign compliance without attack, and (ii) robustness under our attack ladder (standard RFA, adaptive multi-phase RFA, and Heretic; Section <a href="#S2" title="2 Threat Model and Attacks ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>). Full settings, hyperparameters, and per-model configs are in Appendix <a href="#A6.SS2" title="F.2 DDO and Auxiliary Mechanism Hyperparameters (Llama-3) ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Models and baselines.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our primary evaluation uses Llama-3-8B-Instruct with the full attack ladder and baseline comparison. On Llama-3, we compare against six trained defenses using publicly released checkpoints: Circuit Breakers <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>, LAT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite>, ReFAT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite>, RepBend <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite>, Triplet, and Triplet-Adv <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>]</cite>. For cross-model generalization, we evaluate DDO on five additional instruction-tuned model families and compare against four trained baselines (Circuit Breakers, RepBend, LAT, ReFAT) with small hyperparameter sweeps (3–5 configs per defense per model; Appendix <a href="#A6.SS8" title="F.8 Baseline Sweep Details ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.8</span></a>). Seven further models are evaluated with DDO only (Appendix <a href="#A6.SS15" title="F.15 Additional Model Evaluation ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.15</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Evaluation protocol.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All generations use deterministic greedy decoding on a single A100 GPU. Hyperparameter tuning and DIM estimation use a held-out validation split (128 harmful + 128 safe probes); all reported metrics are on held-out test sets. We report knowledge accuracy (MMLU <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">36</a>]</cite>, 5-shot), conversational quality (MT-Bench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">37</a>]</cite>), over-refusal on prompts that superficially resemble harmful ones (XSTest <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">38</a>]</cite>, 250 such prompts, GPT-4o judge), and robustness under DirectRequest (harmful prompts sent directly), four standard-RFA variants (Section <a href="#S2" title="2 Threat Model and Attacks ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>), adaptive multi-phase RFA (up to 8 phases), Heretic (200 trials), and prompt-level jailbreaks (HumanJailbreaks, GCG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite>, PAIR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>]</cite>, AutoDAN <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>]</cite>). Unless otherwise specified, ASR is averaged over three judges: HarmBench classifier <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>]</cite>, LlamaGuard-2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">39</a>]</cite>, and StrongREJECT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">40</a>]</cite>. Configurations that fail a coherence check (non-empty, non-degenerate, minimum-length outputs on 10 benign prompts) are marked “<math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>” and excluded. Full details on decoding, DIM estimation, splits, and benchmark settings are in Appendix <a href="#A6.SS7" title="F.7 Benchmark Settings ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.7</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Results</h3>

<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Standard RFA and Heretic on Llama-3.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ Standard RFA and Heretic on Llama-3. ‣ 4.2 Results ‣ 4 Experiments and Results ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> compares DDO against six trained baselines on Llama-3-8B-Instruct. DDO here denotes DDO (rank 1): one decoy neuron per layer with a single shared reader <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>. <span id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">DDO + debiasing</span> adds orthogonal debiasing (Section <a href="#S3.SS0.SSS0.Px9" title="Orthogonal debiasing (utility repair). ‣ 3 Method: Decoy Direction Optimization (DDO) ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>) to repair over-refusal.
On standard RFA, DDO achieves <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.8\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.8</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.8\%</annotation></semantics></math> mean ASR, comparable to the strongest trained baselines while requiring no finetuning and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\sim}2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\sim}2</annotation></semantics></math> minutes per optimization run. Several trained defenses reduce ASR partly by over-refusing (LAT: <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20.8\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>20.8</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20.8\%</annotation></semantics></math> XSTest; ReFAT: <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="60.4\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>60.4</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60.4\%</annotation></semantics></math>), while DDO preserves <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="91.6\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>91.6</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">91.6\%</annotation></semantics></math>. Adding orthogonal debiasing restores XSTest to <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="99.2\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>99.2</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">99.2\%</annotation></semantics></math> and improves standard RFA further (mean ASR <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.0\%</annotation></semantics></math>). Under Heretic <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">14</a>]</cite> (weight-level attack), DDO achieves <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="18\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>18</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">18\%</annotation></semantics></math> H-200 ASR; a gap to trained RepBend (<math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.3\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.3</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.3\%</annotation></semantics></math>) remains, consistent with trained defenses distributing refusal more diffusely across parameters.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T2" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 2: </span>Main defense comparison on Llama-3-8B-Instruct. ASR (%, 3-judge avg). MT-B = MT-Bench; XST = XSTest; DR = DirectRequest. RFA: 3p/rs = three-point/residual-stream; J/H = JailbreakBench/HarmBench. H-200 = Heretic at 200 trials. <sup id="S4.T2.7" class="ltx_sup"><math id="S4.T2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dagger" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>†</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dagger</annotation></semantics></math></sup> = post-attack generation degradation (Appendix <a href="#A6.SS1.SSS0.Px4" title="Heretic generation quality. ‣ F.1 Attack Implementation Details ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.1</span></a>). <span id="S4.T2.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-bg-color:#C8E6C9;">best</span> / <span id="S4.T2.9" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#C8E6C9;">good</span> / <span id="S4.T2.10" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#FFCDD2;">poor</span> / <span id="S4.T2.11" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E3F2FD;">ours</span>. DDO matches trained baselines on standard RFA (1.8% avg) at 30–450<math id="S4.T2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> lower cost per configuration without finetuning.</figcaption>

</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Adaptive multi-phase RFA.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Under adaptive multi-phase RFA (phases <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t{=}1,\ldots,8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t{=}1,\ldots,8</annotation></semantics></math>), all evaluated defenses degrade as the attacker re-estimates. Worst-case ASR across phases is comparable across the strongest defenses: RepBend <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite> <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="58\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>58</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">58\%</annotation></semantics></math>, ReFAT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite> <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="60\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>60</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60\%</annotation></semantics></math>, DDO (rank <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math>) <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="65\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>65</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">65\%</annotation></semantics></math>, with Circuit Breakers <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite> weaker at <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="75\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>75</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">75\%</annotation></semantics></math>. We track ASR jointly with utility (MT-Bench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">37</a>]</cite>; Figure <a href="#S4.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ Adaptive multi-phase RFA. ‣ 4.2 Results ‣ 4 Experiments and Results ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>) because ASR alone can be misleading—a defense can lower ASR by degrading generation rather than refusing. At Phase 8, DDO (rank <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math>) preserves MT-Bench at <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5.82" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5.82</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5.82</annotation></semantics></math>, comparable to RepBend (<math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6.17" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>6.17</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6.17</annotation></semantics></math>) and Circuit Breakers (<math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5.90" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5.90</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5.90</annotation></semantics></math>), and substantially better than ReFAT, which collapses to <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.01" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.01</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.01</annotation></semantics></math> (Appendix Table <a href="#A6.T17" title="Table 17 ‣ Attack cost model. ‣ F.10 Adaptive Attack: Exact ASR and MT-Bench by Phase ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">17</span></a>). DDO therefore lands in the same operating regime as the strongest gradient-trained defenses on both worst-case ASR and utility under sustained adaptive attack, despite requiring no finetuning (Appendix Figure <a href="#A6.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ Attack cost model. ‣ F.10 Adaptive Attack: Exact ASR and MT-Bench by Phase ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F3" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2609.16204v1/adaptive_rfa_replot.svg" id="S4.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:333/263;" width="333" height="263"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 3: </span>Adaptive RFA on Llama-3-8B (8 phases). <span id="S4.F3.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Top</span>: attack success rate (<math id="S4.F3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>). <span id="S4.F3.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Bottom</span>: model quality (<math id="S4.F3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\uparrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↑</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\uparrow</annotation></semantics></math>). All defenses see rising ASR under sustained re-estimation: DDO (green) remains coherent (MT-Bench <math id="S4.F3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\geq" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>≥</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\geq</annotation></semantics></math>5.82) but ultimately leaks, while ReFAT (red) attains low ASR partly by collapsing quality to 2.46 at Phase 1.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Cross-model generalization and baseline comparison.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To test generalization, we apply DDO to five additional model families (Yi-1.5, Qwen3, Gemma-2, Mistral, and GLM-4) and compare against four trained baselines per model (Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ Cross-model generalization and baseline comparison. ‣ 4.2 Results ‣ 4 Experiments and Results ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>; Appendix <a href="#A6.SS8" title="F.8 Baseline Sweep Details ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.8</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T3" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 3: </span>Cross-model baseline comparison (ASR %, 3-judge avg).
