</table>
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\mathrm{inter}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>inter</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\mathrm{inter}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the MLP intermediate dimension and <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\odot" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>⊙</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\odot</annotation></semantics></math> is elementwise multiplication. Some models (e.g., Gemma-2) use GeGLU, which replaces <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{silu}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>silu</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{silu}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{gelu}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>gelu</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{gelu}</annotation></semantics></math>; our method applies to both variants.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Edited parameters.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our defenses perform <em id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">offline</em> edits to selected parameter matrices, including <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{q},\mathbf{W}_{k},\mathbf{W}_{v},\mathbf{W}_{o},\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{gate}},\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{up}},\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>gate</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>up</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>down</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{q},\mathbf{W}_{k},\mathbf{W}_{v},\mathbf{W}_{o},\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{gate}},\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{up}},\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}</annotation></semantics></math>, the embedding matrix <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{emb}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>emb</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{emb}}</annotation></semantics></math>, the output head <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{lm}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>lm</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{lm}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and (for normalization-based mechanisms) RMSNorm gains <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\boldsymbol{\gamma}_{\ell}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>𝜸</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\boldsymbol{\gamma}_{\ell}\}</annotation></semantics></math>. We fold all edits into these weights before deployment, so defended models run with no architectural or runtime overhead.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Hookpoints (for attacks).</h4>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">When defining RFA variants (Section <a href="#S2" title="2 Threat Model and Attacks ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>), we use three hookpoints per layer: residual-stream input <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{h}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐡</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{h}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>, attention update <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐚</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>, and MLP update <math id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{m}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐦</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{m}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Additional Method Details</h2>

<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1 </span>First-Token Collapse</h3>

<div id="A4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">During DDO optimization, the cross-entropy refusal loss <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{refuse}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>refuse</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{refuse}}</annotation></semantics></math> anchors safety by training the model to produce refusal continuations on harmful prompts. However, this loss operates on the full sequence and can be satisfied by degenerate solutions: the model outputs a compliance-prefixed first token (e.g., “Sure”) to reduce the decoy-confusion loss, then pivots mid-sentence to refusal (e.g., “Sure, I’d be happy to…actually, I cannot assist with that request”). This “first-token collapse” is problematic because (i) autoregressive generation commits to the first token, so a compliance prefix can cascade into full compliance under greedy or sampled decoding, and (ii) ASR judges that inspect only the first few tokens may classify such responses as compliant even though the model eventually refuses.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The refusal-score loss <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{refusal-score}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>refusal-score</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{refusal-score}}</annotation></semantics></math> addresses this by directly supervising first-token logits:</p>
<table id="A4.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{refusal-score}}=\max\!\left(0,\;m-\left[\max_{t\in\mathcal{T}_{\text{ref}}}z_{t}-\max_{t\in\mathcal{T}_{\text{comp}}}z_{t}\right]\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>refusal-score</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:1.808em;" width="1.808em"><mi>max</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi><mtext>ref</mtext></msub></mrow></munder><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi><mtext>comp</mtext></msub></mrow></munder><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{refusal-score}}=\max\!\left(0,\;m-\left[\max_{t\in\mathcal{T}_{\text{ref}}}z_{t}-\max_{t\in\mathcal{T}_{\text{comp}}}z_{t}\right]\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is the logit for token <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{T}_{\text{ref}}=\{\texttt{I},\texttt{Sorry},\texttt{cannot}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi><mtext>ref</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">I</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">Sorry</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">cannot</mtext></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{T}_{\text{ref}}=\{\texttt{I},\texttt{Sorry},\texttt{cannot}\}</annotation></semantics></math> are refusal-prefixed tokens, <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{T}_{\text{comp}}=\{\texttt{Sure},\texttt{Here}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi><mtext>comp</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">Sure</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">Here</mtext></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{T}_{\text{comp}}=\{\texttt{Sure},\texttt{Here}\}</annotation></semantics></math> are compliance-prefixed tokens, and <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> is a margin (<math id="A4.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m{=}0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m{=}0</annotation></semantics></math> in all experiments). This hinge loss ensures that refusal tokens dominate compliance tokens at the first position. In our ablation (Table <a href="#S4.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ Loss components. ‣ 4.3 Ablations ‣ 4 Experiments and Results ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>), removing <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{refusal-score}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>refusal-score</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{refusal-score}}</annotation></semantics></math> increases ASR from 1.8% to 41.8%, confirming that first-token anchoring is essential for DDO’s effectiveness.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.2 </span>All Mechanism Definitions</h3>

<div id="A4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Section <a href="#S3" title="3 Method: Decoy Direction Optimization (DDO) ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> defines DDO (the core mechanism). Here we define the <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="14" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>14</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">14</annotation></semantics></math> additional mechanisms that appear in at least one reported configuration, ablation, or negative-result analysis. Throughout, let <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{\ell}\mathrel{\triangleq}\mathrm{RMSNorm}(\mathbf{h}_{\ell})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mi>RMSNorm</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐡</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{\ell}\mathrel{\triangleq}\mathrm{RMSNorm}(\mathbf{h}_{\ell})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\ell}\mathrel{\triangleq}\mathrm{RMSNorm}(\mathbf{h}_{\ell}^{\mathrm{attn}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mi>RMSNorm</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐡</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>attn</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\ell}\mathrel{\triangleq}\mathrm{RMSNorm}(\mathbf{h}_{\ell}^{\mathrm{attn}})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Decoy Shear Transform (linear baseline).</h4>

<div id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We apply a linear shear that preserves the refusal coordinate but injects orthogonal decoy components: <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{M}_{\ell}\mathrel{\triangleq}\mathbf{I}+\sum_{j}c_{j}\,\mathbf{u}_{\ell,j}\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐌</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mi>𝐈</mi><mo rspace="0.055em">+</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>j</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐮</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{M}_{\ell}\mathrel{\triangleq}\mathbf{I}+\sum_{j}c_{j}\,\mathbf{u}_{\ell,j}\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}_{\ell,j}\perp\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐮</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>⟂</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}_{\ell,j}\perp\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>, folded into <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{o}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{o}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>down</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}</annotation></semantics></math> by left-multiplication. When harmful prompts induce larger <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell},\mathbf{h}\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐡</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell},\mathbf{h}\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> than safe prompts, this shear adds a harmful-selective shift in decoy directions and can rotate the initial DIM estimate away from the causal refusal feature. However, because the transformation is linear, an adaptive attacker can re-estimate DIM on the defended checkpoint and recover the new contrast; on Llama-3 this yields <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="92\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>92</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">92\%</annotation></semantics></math> ASR (3-point RFA, LlamaGuard-2).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Diverse Q-Head Routing.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each attention head <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>, we define a head-specific trigger <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{t}}_{\ell,h}=\cos(\theta)\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}+\sin(\theta)\hat{\mathbf{o}}_{\ell,h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐭</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐨</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{t}}_{\ell,h}=\cos(\theta)\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}+\sin(\theta)\hat{\mathbf{o}}_{\ell,h}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{o}}_{\ell,h}\perp\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐨</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mo>⟂</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{o}}_{\ell,h}\perp\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>, and apply the rank-1 update</p>
<table id="A4.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}^{(h)}_{q,\ell}\leftarrow\mathbf{W}^{(h)}_{q,\ell}+\alpha(\mathbf{W}^{(h)}_{q,\ell}\hat{\mathbf{t}}_{\ell,h})\hat{\mathbf{t}}_{\ell,h}^{\top}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐭</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐭</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}^{(h)}_{q,\ell}\leftarrow\mathbf{W}^{(h)}_{q,\ell}+\alpha(\mathbf{W}^{(h)}_{q,\ell}\hat{\mathbf{t}}_{\ell,h})\hat{\mathbf{t}}_{\ell,h}^{\top}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">This makes different heads respond to slightly different rotations of refusal, aiming to distribute harmful–safe separation across head-specific subspaces. Since attention includes a softmax nonlinearity, such diversification could in principle make the overall behavior harder to summarize by a single residual-stream DIM direction; in practice the edit is brittle and often fails the coherence check on some architectures.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">RoPE Dimension Amplification.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We rescale selected rotary frequencies <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega_{\ell,j}\leftarrow\rho\,\omega_{\ell,j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ω</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ω</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega_{\ell,j}\leftarrow\rho\,\omega_{\ell,j}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j\in\mathcal{J}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒥</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j\in\mathcal{J}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho&gt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho&gt;1</annotation></semantics></math>, by editing the RoPE parameters used by <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{q}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>. If refusal-related computation relies on consistent attention patterns across positions, increasing rotation rates in a subset of dimensions can induce more position-dependent variation, potentially smearing harmful–safe differences across tokens and weakening a simple DIM estimator. This mechanism is highly architecture-sensitive and often degrades generation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Value-Projection Conditioning.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We add a rank-1 component to the value projection, <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{v,\ell}\leftarrow\mathbf{W}_{v,\ell}+\alpha\,\hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\ell}\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{v,\ell}\leftarrow\mathbf{W}_{v,\ell}+\alpha\,\hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\ell}\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> is a fixed random unit vector. This explicitly routes the refusal coordinate <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell},\mathbf{x}\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell},\mathbf{x}\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> into the value stream, so that even if an attacker partially removes refusal by ablating a mis-estimated direction, any surviving refusal signal is amplified and broadcast through attention aggregation downstream. This edit is attention-sensitive and can break coherence on some models.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">KV Rank-1 Strengthening.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This uses the same update as Value-Projection Conditioning but with a larger coefficient <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math>, applied only in late layers (L26–31 on Llama-3) where refusal is strongest: <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{v,\ell}\leftarrow\mathbf{W}_{v,\ell}+\eta\,\hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\ell}\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{v,\ell}\leftarrow\mathbf{W}_{v,\ell}+\eta\,\hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\ell}\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>. Concentrating the coupling where refusal is already causally active makes small ablation errors more consequential, because any residual refusal coordinate is immediately injected into the value stream in the final computation stages.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Head Amplification.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We score heads by <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{\ell,h}=\left\lVert\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}^{\top}\mathbf{W}^{(h)}_{o,\ell}\right\rVert_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mo>‖</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐖</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{\ell,h}=\left\lVert\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}^{\top}\mathbf{W}^{(h)}_{o,\ell}\right\rVert_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, select the top-<math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>, and scale those head outputs by a factor <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> (e.g., <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k{=}4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k{=}4</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma{=}2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma{=}2</annotation></semantics></math>). If a subset of heads carries disproportionate refusal-aligned signal, amplifying them increases the magnitude of refusal-correlated residual updates, so a fixed-strength (or mis-targeted) ablation leaves more refusal behind. Because it edits <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{o}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{o}</annotation></semantics></math> (part of Heretic’s weight-edit surface), this mechanism is mostly a control for standard RFA rather than a robust defense.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px7" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Autoregressive Embedding Boost.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For refusal-prefix tokens <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in\{\texttt{I},\texttt{cannot},\texttt{can},\texttt{'t},\texttt{Sorry}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">I</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">cannot</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">can</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">’t</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">Sorry</mtext></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in\{\texttt{I},\texttt{cannot},\texttt{can},\texttt{'t},\texttt{Sorry}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, we add a small refusal-aligned component to their embeddings: <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px7.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{emb}}[t,:]\mathrel{+}=\alpha\,\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\mathrm{avg}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>emb</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mo rspace="0em">:</mo><mo rspace="0.056em" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">+</mo><mo lspace="0em">=</mo><mi>α</mi><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>avg</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{emb}}[t,:]\mathrel{+}=\alpha\,\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\mathrm{avg}}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\mathrm{avg}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>avg</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\mathrm{avg}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the layer-averaged refusal direction. Once generation begins with a refusal prefix, the boosted embedding injects extra refusal signal at the next step, creating a positive feedback loop that can make refusal harder to interrupt if an attacker has only partially removed refusal features.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px8" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">RMSNorm Gain Control.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We increase RMSNorm gain on the top-<math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> refusal-aligned channels: <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma_{\ell,j}\leftarrow g\,\gamma_{\ell,j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>γ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_{\ell,j}\leftarrow g\,\gamma_{\ell,j}</annotation></semantics></math> for indices <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px8.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> with the largest <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px8.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell,j}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell,j}|</annotation></semantics></math>. RMSNorm applies state-dependent rescaling (<math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px8.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{y}=\mathbf{x}/\mathrm{RMS}(\mathbf{x})\odot\boldsymbol{\gamma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>RMS</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⊙</mo><mi>𝜸</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{y}=\mathbf{x}/\mathrm{RMS}(\mathbf{x})\odot\boldsymbol{\gamma}</annotation></semantics></math>), so amplifying refusal-aligned channels changes the effective coupling between channels in a data-dependent way. This could make harmful–safe differences less well described by a fixed linear direction; in practice, such edits often destabilize generation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px9" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Orthogonal Debiasing (utility repair).</h4>

<div id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We estimate an over-refusal direction <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{v}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐯</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{v}}</annotation></semantics></math> from benign prompts the model incorrectly refuses (constructed to be approximately orthogonal to <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px9.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>), and remove sensitivity to <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px9.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{v}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐯</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{v}}</annotation></semantics></math> by projecting it out of selected matrices: <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px9.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}^{\prime}=\mathbf{W}-(\mathbf{W}\hat{\mathbf{v}})\hat{\mathbf{v}}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝐖</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐯</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐯</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}^{\prime}=\mathbf{W}-(\mathbf{W}\hat{\mathbf{v}})\hat{\mathbf{v}}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math> for input-dimension matrices (<math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px9.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{emb}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>emb</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{emb}}</annotation></semantics></math>), and <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px9.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}^{\prime}=\mathbf{W}-\hat{\mathbf{v}}(\hat{\mathbf{v}}^{\top}\mathbf{W})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝐖</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐯</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐯</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐖</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}^{\prime}=\mathbf{W}-\hat{\mathbf{v}}(\hat{\mathbf{v}}^{\top}\mathbf{W})</annotation></semantics></math> for output-dimension matrices (<math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px9.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{o}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{o}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px9.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>down</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}</annotation></semantics></math>). Since DDO can mildly increase benign refusals on some models, removing the dominant benign-bias direction repairs compliance without directly weakening refusal, because the edited direction is chosen to be orthogonal to refusal.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px10" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Refusal Direction Rotation.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px10.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px10.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We apply a fixed Givens rotation in the <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px10.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\hat{\mathbf{r}},\mathbf{v}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐯</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\hat{\mathbf{r}},\mathbf{v}\}</annotation></semantics></math> plane (<math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px10.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta=\pi/3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta=\pi/3</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px10.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}\perp\hat{\mathbf{r}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐯</mi><mo>⟂</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}\perp\hat{\mathbf{r}}</annotation></semantics></math>), folded into <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px10.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{o}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{o}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px10.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>down</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}</annotation></semantics></math>. This can appear to “hide” refusal by moving it away from <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px10.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{r}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{r}}</annotation></semantics></math>, but the rotated refusal direction <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px10.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{def}}=\mathbf{M}\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{base}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐫</mi><mi>def</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝐌𝐫</mi><mi>base</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{def}}=\mathbf{M}\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{base}}</annotation></semantics></math> is still a single linear direction, so an adaptive attacker can re-estimate DIM on the defended checkpoint and recover it (Llama-3: <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px10.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="68\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>68</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">68\%</annotation></semantics></math> ASR).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px11" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Representation Rerouting.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px11.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px11.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We learn a rank-<math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px11.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math> update <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px11.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\mathbf{W}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐖</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\mathbf{W}</annotation></semantics></math> (applied to <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px11.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{o}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{o}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px11.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>down</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}</annotation></semantics></math>) that maps harmful activations toward random target representations. If harmful activations are pushed into a more diverse set of directions, the harmful–safe contrast could become less low-rank, weakening rank-1 DIM estimation. In practice, harmful and safe activations remain linearly separable after rerouting, so a re-estimated DIM direction still removes refusal (Llama-3: <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px11.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="86\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>86</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">86\%</annotation></semantics></math> ASR).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px12" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Refusal Scattering.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px12.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px12.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We attempt to distribute the refusal direction across <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px12.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k{=}8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k{=}8</annotation></semantics></math> random orthogonal residual directions (via rank-<math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px12.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> perturbations to <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px12.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{o}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{o}</annotation></semantics></math>) and boost refusal-prefix logits via LM-head scaling. If refusal were spread across multiple orthogonal directions, a rank-1 ablation would remove only a fraction of it, forcing the attacker to use higher rank or more phases. In practice, this approach performed poorly in early tests and we did not evaluate it beyond a coherence check.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px13" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">LM-Head Multiplicative Row Scaling.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px13.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px13.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We reshape a small set of logits by multiplicatively rescaling corresponding LM-head rows. For selected token IDs <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px13.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> (refusal-prefix tokens such as “I/cannot/can” and compliance tokens such as “’d/would/Sure/Here”), we apply</p>
<table id="A4.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E11.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{lm}}[t,:]\leftarrow s_{t}\,\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{lm}}[t,:]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>lm</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mo rspace="0em">:</mo><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>lm</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mo rspace="0em">:</mo><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{lm}}[t,:]\leftarrow s_{t}\,\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{lm}}[t,:],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px13.p1.2" class="ltx_p">which rescales <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px13.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="z_{t}=\langle\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{lm}}[t,:],\mathbf{h}\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>lm</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mo rspace="0em">:</mo><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐡</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}=\langle\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{lm}}[t,:],\mathbf{h}\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> without modifying hidden-state activations. Since RFA-like attacks operate on hidden states, changing the LM head can provide additional refusal “headroom” even if intermediate refusal features are partially reduced. We tune <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px13.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{s_{t}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{s_{t}\}</annotation></semantics></math> with Optuna <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px14" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Adversarial Sign Coupling.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px14.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px14.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We repurpose a small set of SwiGLU units to implement a <em id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px14.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">bilinear</em> cross-term between the refusal coordinate and an orthogonal coordinate. In layer <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px14.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>, sample <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px14.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{o}}_{\ell}\perp\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐨</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>⟂</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{o}}_{\ell}\perp\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> and choose a small set of intermediate units <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px14.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> disjoint from the gated-decoy units (we use a fixed neuron-index offset, 30+). We set each unit so that its gate row aligns with <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px14.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{o}}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐨</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{o}}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> and its up row aligns with <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px14.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>, while its down column writes into a fixed random output direction <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px14.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}_{\ell,i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐮</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}_{\ell,i}</annotation></semantics></math>. The resulting contribution is</p>
<table id="A4.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{i}(\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\ell})=\operatorname{silu}(\langle\hat{\mathbf{o}}_{\ell},\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\ell}\rangle)\cdot\langle\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell},\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\ell}\rangle\cdot\mathbf{u}_{\ell,i}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>silu</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐨</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>𝐮</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{i}(\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\ell})=\operatorname{silu}(\langle\hat{\mathbf{o}}_{\ell},\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\ell}\rangle)\cdot\langle\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell},\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\ell}\rangle\cdot\mathbf{u}_{\ell,i}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px14.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Adaptive multi-phase RFA repeatedly estimates and ablates a <em id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px14.p1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">linear</em> DIM direction at fixed hookpoints. Because the sign-coupled term depends on the <em id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px14.p1.2.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">product</em> of two coordinates, the effective linear surrogate presented by this bilinear feature can shift after ablation and across hookpoints, potentially increasing the number of distinct directions (phases/rank) an attacker must remove to fully suppress refusal-related computation.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Theoretical Proofs and Formalizations</h2>

<section id="A5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.1 </span>Proofs of the Overlap and Spectral Bounds</h3>

<div id="A5.SS1.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof of Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 1 (Subspace overlap bound). ‣ Spectral analysis of contrastive ablation. ‣ 3 Method: Decoy Direction Optimization (DDO) ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.</h6>
<div id="A5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{k}=Q_{k}(C)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{k}=Q_{k}(C)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> contain the top-<math id="A5.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> left and right singular vectors of <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively, and let <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma_{k}=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_{1}(C),\ldots,\sigma_{k}(C))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>diag</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma_{k}=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_{1}(C),\ldots,\sigma_{k}(C))</annotation></semantics></math>. The SVD identity <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="CV_{k}=Q_{k}\Sigma_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">CV_{k}=Q_{k}\Sigma_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> gives</span></p>
<table id="A5.Ex9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.Ex9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pi_{\mathcal{R}}Q_{k}=\Pi_{\mathcal{R}}CV_{k}\Sigma_{k}^{-1}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pi_{\mathcal{R}}Q_{k}=\Pi_{\mathcal{R}}CV_{k}\Sigma_{k}^{-1},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text">where <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> is invertible because <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{k}(C)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{k}(C)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> have orthonormal columns,</span></p>

<p id="A5.SS1.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text">∎</span></p>

<div id="A5.SS1.3" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof of Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 2 (Overlap bound under orthogonal decoys). ‣ Decoy contrast decomposition. ‣ 3 Method: Decoy Direction Optimization (DDO) ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>.</h6>
<div id="A5.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Because <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U^{\top}U=I_{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>U</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>U</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U^{\top}U=I_{m}</annotation></semantics></math>, the nonzero singular values of <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{\theta}=UA_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{\theta}=UA_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> equal those of <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>. Weyl’s singular-value inequality and <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pi_{\mathcal{R}}U=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>U</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pi_{\mathcal{R}}U=0</annotation></semantics></math> give</span></p>

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A5.Ex11Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\|\Pi_{\mathcal{R}}C_{\theta}\|_{\mathrm{op}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>op</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\|\Pi_{\mathcal{R}}C_{\theta}\|_{\mathrm{op}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="A5.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">Substitution into Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 1 (Subspace overlap bound). ‣ Spectral analysis of contrastive ablation. ‣ 3 Method: Decoy Direction Optimization (DDO) ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> proves the bound. If <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\leq k\leq r_{\mathrm{eff}}(\varepsilon)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>eff</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ε</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\leq k\leq r_{\mathrm{eff}}(\varepsilon)</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{k}(A_{\theta})-\rho&gt;\rho_{\mathcal{R}}/\varepsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>ρ</mi></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><mi>ε</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{k}(A_{\theta})-\rho&gt;\rho_{\mathcal{R}}/\varepsilon</annotation></semantics></math>, so the overlap is at most <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ε</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS1.4" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof of Corollary <a href="#Thmtheorem3" title="Corollary 3 (Optimal spectrum under an energy constraint). ‣ Decoy energy allocation. ‣ 3 Method: Decoy Direction Optimization (DDO) ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>.</h6>
<div id="A5.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">The singular values are nonincreasing, and their squared sum equals the squared Frobenius norm. Hence</span></p>
<table id="A5.Ex12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.Ex12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\,\sigma_{k}(A_{\theta})^{2}\leq\sum_{j=1}^{k}\sigma_{j}(A_{\theta})^{2}\leq\|A_{\theta}\|_{F}^{2}\leq B^{2}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">≤</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>k</mi></munderover><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>≤</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\,\sigma_{k}(A_{\theta})^{2}\leq\sum_{j=1}^{k}\sigma_{j}(A_{\theta})^{2}\leq\|A_{\theta}\|_{F}^{2}\leq B^{2}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS1.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">Taking square roots gives <math id="A5.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{k}(A_{\theta})\leq B/\sqrt{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>/</mo><msqrt><mi>k</mi></msqrt></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{k}(A_{\theta})\leq B/\sqrt{k}</annotation></semantics></math>. Equality is attained when the first <math id="A5.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> singular values all equal <math id="A5.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B/\sqrt{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>/</mo><msqrt><mi>k</mi></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B/\sqrt{k}</annotation></semantics></math> and every remaining singular value is zero.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="Thmtheorem4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_corollary">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmtheorem4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 4</span></span><span id="Thmtheorem4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Overlap under decoy-dominated contrast)<span id="Thmtheorem4.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmtheorem4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmtheorem4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmtheorem4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">If <math id="Thmtheorem4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C=C_{\mathrm{ref}}+C_{\mathrm{dec}}+E" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>ref</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>dec</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>E</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C=C_{\mathrm{ref}}+C_{\mathrm{dec}}+E</annotation></semantics></math>, with <math id="Thmtheorem4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pi_{\mathcal{R}}C_{\mathrm{dec}}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>dec</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pi_{\mathcal{R}}C_{\mathrm{dec}}=0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="Thmtheorem4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|C_{\mathrm{ref}}+E\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq s_{\mathrm{ref}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>ref</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>E</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>op</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>ref</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|C_{\mathrm{ref}}+E\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq s_{\mathrm{ref}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="Thmtheorem4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{k}(C_{\mathrm{dec}})\geq s_{\mathrm{dec}}&gt;s_{\mathrm{ref}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>dec</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>dec</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>ref</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{k}(C_{\mathrm{dec}})\geq s_{\mathrm{dec}}&gt;s_{\mathrm{ref}}</annotation></semantics></math>, then</span></p>
<table id="A5.E13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<section id="A5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.2 </span>Stackelberg Formulation</h3>

<div id="A5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We formalize the defender–attacker interaction as a capability-constrained Stackelberg game.</p>
</div>
<section id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Setup.</h4>

<div id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The defender commits to a post-training weight edit <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta\in\Theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta\in\Theta</annotation></semantics></math>, producing checkpoint <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>. After observing <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>, the attacker chooses an attack <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a\in\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a\in\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math> (e.g., rank-<math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> RFA, <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math>-phase adaptive RFA, <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>-trial Heretic) to maximize harmful compliance while preserving capability:</p>

</table>
<p id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[x]_{+}\mathrel{\triangleq}\max(x,0)" display="inline" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ASR</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U(\theta,a)</annotation></semantics></math> is a utility proxy (e.g., MT-Bench), <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> is an attacker utility threshold, <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda\geq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda\geq 0</annotation></semantics></math> controls the capability–compliance tradeoff, and <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c(a)" The defender solves</p>

<p id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{BR}_{\lambda,\tau}(\theta)=\arg\max_{a\in\mathcal{A}}u_{A}(\theta,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>BR</mi><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{BR}_{\lambda,\tau}(\theta)=\arg\max_{a\in\mathcal{A}}u_{A}(\theta,a)</annotation></semantics></math> is the attacker’s best response, <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>μ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu</annotation></semantics></math> penalizes defender utility violations, <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>D</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{D}</annotation></semantics></math> is the defender’s utility floor (without attack), and <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{D}(\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{D}(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> is editing cost.</p>

<div id="Thmtheorem5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmtheorem5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 5</span></span><span id="Thmtheorem5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Capability-constrained ASR and deterrence)<span id="Thmtheorem5.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmtheorem5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmtheorem5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmtheorem5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For defense <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>, utility threshold <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>, and attack family <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></p>
<table id="A5.E16" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
