<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(16)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="Thmtheorem5.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmtheorem5.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">We say <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(q,\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(q,\tau)</annotation></semantics></math><em id="Thmtheorem5.p1.2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_upright">-deterrent</em> against <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math> if <math id="Thmtheorem5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{CC\text{-}ASR}_{\tau}(\theta)&lt;q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>CC</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">-</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ASR</mi><mi>τ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{CC\text{-}ASR}_{\tau}(\theta)&lt;q</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">CC-ASR separates clean jailbreaks (high ASR with preserved utility) from pyrrhic failures (high ASR with destroyed utility). Worst-case ASR conflates these; CC-ASR isolates the deployment-relevant threat.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Implications for capability-constrained attacks.</h4>

<div id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Consider a family of contrastive attacks satisfying the assumptions of Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 2 (Overlap bound under orthogonal decoys). ‣ Decoy contrast decomposition. ‣ 3 Method: Decoy Direction Optimization (DDO) ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>. If every capability-preserving attack in this family has rank at most <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\mathrm{eff}}(\varepsilon)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>eff</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ε</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\mathrm{eff}}(\varepsilon)</annotation></semantics></math> (the effective decoy rank), then its causal overlap is at most <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ε</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon</annotation></semantics></math>. Assuming further that the increase in expected compliance is at most <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> times this overlap gives <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{CC\text{-}ASR}_{\tau}(\theta)\leq A(\theta,\varnothing)+L\varepsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>CC</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>-</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ASR</mi><mi>τ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∅</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ε</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{CC\text{-}ASR}_{\tau}(\theta)\leq A(\theta,\varnothing)+L\varepsilon</annotation></semantics></math> for that family. Here <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> is a modeling assumption for a smooth expected compliance rate, rather than discrete empirical ASR. For a given attack rank <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>, DDO therefore seeks to maximize the spectral margin <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{k}(A_{\theta})-\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>ρ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{k}(A_{\theta})-\rho</annotation></semantics></math> subject to utility constraints.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Stopping criterion for adaptive RFA.</h4>

<div id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For adaptive multi-phase RFA, let <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> denote ASR, utility, and cumulative attack cost after phase <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>. Under a one-step comparison, continuing from phase <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t+1</annotation></semantics></math> is beneficial when</p>
<table id="A5.Ex14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.Ex14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{t+1}-A_{t}&gt;\lambda\bigl([\tau-U_{t+1}]_{+}-[\tau-U_{t}]_{+}\bigr)+(c_{t+1}-c_{t})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>U</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo></msub></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{t+1}-A_{t}&gt;\lambda\bigl([\tau-U_{t+1}]_{+}-[\tau-U_{t}]_{+}\bigr)+(c_{t+1}-c_{t}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The marginal ASR gain must exceed the added capability penalty and attack cost. DDO aims to shift substantial ASR gains to later phases, where capability degradation can outweigh them. Empirically (Figure <a href="#S4.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ Adaptive multi-phase RFA. ‣ 4.2 Results ‣ 4 Experiments and Results ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>), DDO (rank <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math>) maintains MT-Bench <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\geq 5.82" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≥</mo><mn>5.82</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\geq 5.82</annotation></semantics></math> through Phase <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math>, comparable to RepBend (<math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6.17" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>6.17</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6.17</annotation></semantics></math>) and Circuit Breakers (<math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5.90" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5.90</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5.90</annotation></semantics></math>); ReFAT drops to MT-Bench <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.46" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.46</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.46</annotation></semantics></math> at Phase <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>, so its low ASR is bought at the cost of utility under this formulation.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.3 </span>Empirical Spectral Analysis</h3>

<div id="A5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We empirically validate the flat-spectrum tradeoff predicted by Corollary <a href="#Thmtheorem3" title="Corollary 3 (Optimal spectrum under an energy constraint). ‣ Decoy energy allocation. ‣ 3 Method: Decoy Direction Optimization (DDO) ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>. We train DDO with <math id="A5.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K\in\{1,2,4,8\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K\in\{1,2,4,8\}</annotation></semantics></math> decoy neurons per layer, each with a <em id="A5.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">diversified reader</em> (distinct trigger direction via random orthogonal perturbation). Without diversified readers, all <math id="A5.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> neurons read the same scalar <math id="A5.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell},\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\ell}\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\ell},\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\ell}\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> is effectively rank 1 regardless of <math id="A5.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>. With diversified readers, each neuron reads a different coordinate, giving <math id="A5.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> up to <math id="A5.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> significant singular values. We then attack each model with rank-<math id="A5.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> SVD ablation (Table <a href="#A5.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ E.3 Empirical Spectral Analysis ‣ Appendix E Theoretical Proofs and Formalizations ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<figure id="A5.T6" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 6: </span><span id="A5.T6.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Diversified-reader DDO under rank-<math id="A5.T6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> attacks (ASR %<math id="A5.T6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>, LlamaGuard-2, Llama-3-8B). <math id="A5.T6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> = decoy neurons per layer; <math id="A5.T6.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> = attack rank. As predicted by Corollary <a href="#Thmtheorem3" title="Corollary 3 (Optimal spectrum under an energy constraint). ‣ Decoy energy allocation. ‣ 3 Method: Decoy Direction Optimization (DDO) ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, increasing <math id="A5.T6.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> weakens rank-1 protection (energy spread) but strengthens higher-rank protection (more decoy directions to exhaust).</span></figcaption>

<div id="A5.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Three patterns confirm the corollary: (i) <em id="A5.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">rank-1 protection weakens with <math id="A5.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math></em>: ASR rises from 10% (<math id="A5.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}1</annotation></semantics></math>) to 27% (<math id="A5.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}4</annotation></semantics></math>) as energy is spread across more directions; (ii) <em id="A5.SS3.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">higher-rank protection strengthens</em>: at <math id="A5.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k{=}16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k{=}16</annotation></semantics></math>, ASR drops from 5% (<math id="A5.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}1</annotation></semantics></math>) to 2% (<math id="A5.SS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{\geq}2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{\geq}2</annotation></semantics></math>); and (iii) <math id="A5.SS3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}2</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A5.SS3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math> provides the best tradeoff (0–1% ASR at <math id="A5.SS3.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k{=}2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k{=}2</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A5.SS3.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> with moderate rank-1 cost).</p>
</div>
<section id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">

<div id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">

<p id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Diversified readers reduce <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{1}/\sigma_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{1}/\sigma_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> from 934:1 (single reader, effective rank 1) to 15:1 (diversified, effective rank <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>&gt;</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;</annotation></semantics></math>1), directly confirming that reader diversification flattens the decoy spectrum as predicted.</p>

<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Full Experimental Details</h2>

<section id="A6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.1 </span>Attack Implementation Details</h3>

<section id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Standard RFA.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We compute per-layer DIM directions at the last token position: for each layer <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\ell}=\mathrm{normalize}(\bar{\mathbf{h}}_{\ell}^{\mathrm{harm}}-\bar{\mathbf{h}}_{\ell}^{\mathrm{safe}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐝</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>normalize</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐡</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>harm</mi></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐡</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>safe</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\ell}=\mathrm{normalize}(\bar{\mathbf{h}}_{\ell}^{\mathrm{harm}}-\bar{\mathbf{h}}_{\ell}^{\mathrm{safe}})</annotation></semantics></math> where <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\mathbf{h}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐡</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\mathbf{h}}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the mean activation over the probe set. Mean activations are accumulated in float64 for numerical stability. All <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math> per-layer directions are applied simultaneously via forward hooks (three-point: block input + attention output + MLP output; residual-stream: block input only). This differs from the Arditi et al. direction <em id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">selection</em> pipeline <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>]</cite>, which selects a single (position, layer) direction by evaluating each candidate using KL divergence on safe prompts. Our per-layer procedure corresponds to a larger ablation budget (one direction per layer) and is therefore at least as strong as the single-direction variant under matched probe sets. For all reported results we use <span id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">unfiltered</span> DIM estimation (no refusal-score filtering of the probe set), which provides the attacker with a cleaner direction estimate.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Adaptive multi-phase RFA.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">At each phase <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, we collect activations with all prior phases’ hooks active, compute fresh per-layer DIM directions, and Gram-Schmidt orthogonalize against all previous directions. All <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> direction sets are then ablated simultaneously using three-point hooks. Total hookpoints: up to <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3tL" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3tL</annotation></semantics></math> per forward pass (<math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math> hookpoints <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> phases <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L{=}32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L{=}32</annotation></semantics></math> layers). The attack is deterministic: three identical runs produce identical direction sequences. We evaluate up to <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> phases.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Heretic <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">14</a>]</cite>.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We run the released Heretic tool in an isolated Python virtual environment via subprocess. Key settings: Optuna TPE sampler with <span id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">n_startup_trials=15</span>, <span id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">n_ei_candidates=128</span>, <span id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">multivariate=True</span>. Multi-objective optimization: minimize <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\text{refusals},\text{KL divergence})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mtext>refusals</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext>KL divergence</mtext><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\text{refusals},\text{KL divergence})</annotation></semantics></math>. The tool optimizes a peaked per-layer ablation strength profile <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha(\ell)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha(\ell)</annotation></semantics></math> over <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{o}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{o}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>down</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}</annotation></semantics></math> matrices. We report results at <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="200" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>200</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">200</annotation></semantics></math> trials (H-200). Direction scope is searched over “global” (single direction index) and “per_layer”. Per-component search ranges: <span id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">max_weight</span> <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\in[0.8,1.5]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0.8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\in[0.8,1.5]</annotation></semantics></math>, <span id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">max_weight_position</span> <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\in[0.6L,L]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>0.6</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\in[0.6L,L]</annotation></semantics></math>, <span id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">min_weight</span> <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\in[0,1]\times\texttt{max\_weight}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">max_weight</mtext></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\in[0,1]\times\texttt{max\_weight}</annotation></semantics></math>, <span id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">min_weight_distance</span> <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\in[1,0.6L]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>0.6</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\in[1,0.6L]</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Heretic generation quality.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Daggered entries in Tables <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ Standard RFA and Heretic on Llama-3. ‣ 4.2 Results ‣ 4 Experiments and Results ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> and <a href="#A6.T18" title="Table 18 ‣ F.11 Extended Model Comparison ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a> indicate post-attack generation degradation associated with KL divergence <math id="A6.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0.3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;0.3</annotation></semantics></math> in the selected Heretic trial. Heretic’s KL metric measures the change in output probability distributions on benign prompts relative to the checkpoint before attack. It provides a diagnostic of distributional change rather than a direct measure of task accuracy. The utility columns in these tables describe the defended checkpoints before attack; they do not measure post-Heretic utility.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">

<div id="A6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">

All mechanisms share the same unfiltered DIM estimation protocol and probe budget.</p>
</div>

<section id="A6.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.3 </span>Per-Model Causal Refusal Zones</h3>

<div id="A6.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To choose DDO layers, we estimate each model’s causal refusal zone via single-layer ablations. For each layer <math id="A6.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>, we ablate only the per-layer DIM direction at <math id="A6.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math> (3-point hooks) and measure the resulting drop in refusal rate (substring heuristic) on <math id="A6.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math> harmful prompts. We classify a layer as “causal” if the refusal drop exceeds <math id="A6.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10\%</annotation></semantics></math>. Table <a href="#A6.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ F.3 Per-Model Causal Refusal Zones ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> reports the resulting causal zones and DDO placement for all <math id="A6.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7</annotation></semantics></math> models. “Causal Zone” is the span from the earliest to the latest causal layer; #C is the number of layers within that span that exceed the <math id="A6.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10\%</annotation></semantics></math> threshold (not necessarily contiguous—e.g., Llama-2 has <math id="A6.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math> causal layers scattered across L13–31); and Frac is #C divided by the total number of layers. The upstream placement principle (Section <a href="#S3.SS0.SSS0.Px5" title="Layer placement. ‣ 3 Method: Decoy Direction Optimization (DDO) ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>) suggests that, on localized models, DDO layers should start at or before the causal zone (allowing partial overlap).</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.T9" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 9: </span>Causal refusal zones, DDO placement, and compile mode across all <math id="A6.T9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7</annotation></semantics></math> models. #C = number of causal layers; Frac = fraction of total layers that are causal. Compile mode does not follow a simple redundancy rule: Mistral has <math id="A6.T9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="81\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>81</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">81\%</annotation></semantics></math> causal fraction (distributed) yet requires additive because replace inverts its refusal signal (Table <a href="#A6.T12" title="Table 12 ‣ F.5 Layer Placement Analysis ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a>).</figcaption>
<table id="A6.T9.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">

</section>
<section id="A6.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.4 </span>Compile Mode Selection Details</h3>

<div id="A6.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We compile DDO parameters into model weights using one of two modes: (i) <span id="A6.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">replace</span> (<span id="A6.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">.copy_()</span>), which completely overwrites the neuron’s row/column vectors with the decoy trigger and output (a clean, high-magnitude decoy signal, but it removes the neuron’s original computation), and (ii) <span id="A6.SS4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">additive</span> (<span id="A6.SS4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">.add_()</span>), which adds the decoy signal on top of the original neuron weights (preserves original behavior, but yields a weaker, mixed decoy signal).</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The preferred mode depends on how each model’s refusal circuitry responds to neuron overwriting, rather than a simple redundancy rule:</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.T10" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 10: </span>DDO compile mode comparison across 7 models (ASR %<math id="A6.T10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>, mean of 4 RFA variants, 3-judge avg, 15 Optuna trials per mode). <span id="A6.T10.5" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#C8E6C9;">best</span> / <span id="A6.T10.6" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#FFCDD2;">poor</span> / <span id="A6.T10.7" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E3F2FD;">ours</span>; <math id="A6.T10.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> = coherence failure. The preferred mode is model-specific; replace is stronger when tolerated but breaks some architectures.</figcaption>

<th id="A6.T10.8.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt"><span id="A6.T10.8.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Gate</span></th>

<div id="A6.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Replace mode produces a stronger decoy signal but is more disruptive: overwriting a neuron’s weights removes its original computation. On some models this eliminates baseline refusal entirely (Mistral: <math id="A6.SS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\%</annotation></semantics></math> Ref under replace; Table <a href="#A6.T12" title="Table 12 ‣ F.5 Layer Placement Analysis ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a>), while on others the model compensates (Yi: <math id="A6.SS4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="93\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>93</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">93\%</annotation></semantics></math> Ref despite replacement). Gemma-2 (GeGLU) fails the coherence check under replace entirely. Additive mode preserves the original neuron and superposes the decoy, making it safer but producing a weaker, mixed decoy signal. Note that the closed-form decoy contribution (Equation <a href="#S3.E2" title="In Gated decoy architecture. ‣ 3 Method: Decoy Direction Optimization (DDO) ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>) is exact only under replace mode; in additive mode, the SwiGLU nonlinearity produces cross-terms between the original and inserted weights, so Equation <a href="#S3.E2" title="In Gated decoy architecture. ‣ 3 Method: Decoy Direction Optimization (DDO) ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> should be interpreted as the intended decoy component rather than the exact neuron output. In practice, we evaluate both modes and select by ASR subject to passing the coherence check.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.5 </span>Layer Placement Analysis</h3>

<div id="A6.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">DDO’s effectiveness depends critically on <em id="A6.SS5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">where</em> decoys are placed relative to the model’s causal refusal zone—the layers whose ablation causally reduces refusal (Table <a href="#A6.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ F.3 Per-Model Causal Refusal Zones ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>). Ideally, decoy layers should start at or before the causal zone so that the decoy signal contaminates the attacker’s estimator without disrupting the refusal computation itself.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.T11" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 11: </span>Effect of decoy placement on baseline refusal rate. Refusal rate measured on 100 JailbreakBench behaviors (substring heuristic, without attack). Ref<math id="A6.T11.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{}_{\text{base}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow></mrow><mtext>base</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{}_{\text{base}}</annotation></semantics></math> = undefended model; Ref<math id="A6.T11.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{}_{\text{in}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow></mrow><mtext>in</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{}_{\text{in}}</annotation></semantics></math> = decoys placed inside the causal zone; Ref<math id="A6.T11.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{}_{\text{up}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow></mrow><mtext>up</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{}_{\text{up}}</annotation></semantics></math> = decoys placed upstream.</figcaption>

</figure>
<div id="A6.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A6.T11" title="Table 11 ‣ F.5 Layer Placement Analysis ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a> shows that placement affects baseline refusal: placing decoys <em id="A6.SS5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">inside</em> the causal zone can substantially reduce refusal (e.g., Gemma-2: <math id="A6.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="93\%\rightarrow 68\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>93</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mn>68</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">93\%\rightarrow 68\%</annotation></semantics></math>; Qwen3: <math id="A6.SS5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="37\%\rightarrow 19\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>37</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mn>19</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">37\%\rightarrow 19\%</annotation></semantics></math>; Mistral: <math id="A6.SS5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="58\%\rightarrow 3\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>58</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">58\%\rightarrow 3\%</annotation></semantics></math>), while <em id="A6.SS5.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">upstream</em> placement largely preserves it. On models with distributed or sparse refusal patterns (Yi, Llama-2), placement makes less difference because refusal is redundant or only weakly localized across layers. Placement also affects <em id="A6.SS5.p2.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">ASR under attack</em>: on Qwen3, decoys placed inside the causal zone yield <math id="A6.SS5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="80\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>80</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">80\%</annotation></semantics></math> 3-point RFA ASR (LlamaGuard-2, JailbreakBench) compared to <math id="A6.SS5.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="35\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>35</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">35\%</annotation></semantics></math> for upstream placement, even though baseline refusal is preserved in both cases. This motivates the upstream placement principle: placing decoys at or before the causal zone contaminates the attacker’s estimator without disrupting the refusal computation itself.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A6.T12" title="Table 12 ‣ F.5 Layer Placement Analysis ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> shows how compile mode affects baseline refusal:</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.T12" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 12: </span>Baseline refusal rate (<math id="A6.T12.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\uparrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↑</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\uparrow</annotation></semantics></math>) under DDO replace vs. additive. Refusal rate measured on 100 JailbreakBench behaviors (substring heuristic, without attack). DDO uses per-model Optuna-tuned hyperparams (Table <a href="#A6.T13" title="Table 13 ‣ F.6 Per-Model DDO Best Configs ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>). <span id="A6.T12.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#FFCDD2;">red</span> = refusal disrupted by DDO; <math id="A6.T12.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> = coherence failure. The best compile mode depends on how each model’s refusal circuitry responds to neuron overwriting.</figcaption>
<table id="A6.T12.4" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="A6.T12.4.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A6.T12.4.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt"><span id="A6.T12.4.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Model</span></th>

</figure>
<div id="A6.SS5.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS5.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A6.T12" title="Table 12 ‣ F.5 Layer Placement Analysis ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> reveals why the best compile mode is model-specific: replace mode produces a stronger decoy but can disrupt refusal itself. On Gemma-2, replace fails the coherence check, so additive is selected. On Mistral, replace nearly eliminates refusal (<math id="A6.SS5.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\%</annotation></semantics></math> Ref), explaining its higher ASR with replace vs. additive (Table <a href="#A6.T10" title="Table 10 ‣ F.4 Compile Mode Selection Details ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>). On GLM-4, the pattern reverses: additive disrupts refusal (<math id="A6.SS5.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="38\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>38</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">38\%</annotation></semantics></math> Ref) while replace preserves it (<math id="A6.SS5.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>96</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96\%</annotation></semantics></math>). The best mode therefore depends on how the model’s refusal circuitry responds to neuron overwriting, not on a simple rule.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.6 </span>Per-Model DDO Best Configs</h3>

<div id="A6.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A6.T13" title="Table 13 ‣ F.6 Per-Model DDO Best Configs ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a> reports the DDO hyperparameters used for each model in Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ Cross-model generalization and baseline comparison. ‣ 4.2 Results ‣ 4 Experiments and Results ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>. For each model, we run <math id="A6.SS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>15</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">15</annotation></semantics></math> Optuna trials in replace mode and <math id="A6.SS6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>15</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">15</annotation></semantics></math> in additive mode, selecting the lower-ASR mode subject to a benign-compliance drop of <math id="A6.SS6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&lt;20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&lt;20</annotation></semantics></math> percentage points on held-out validation prompts when feasible. The search space covers layer range, <math id="A6.SS6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> (gate scale), scale (output magnitude), confusion <math id="A6.SS6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math> (estimator-confusion loss weight), learning rate, and number of epochs. Layer ranges are guided by the causal refusal zone (Table <a href="#A6.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ F.3 Per-Model Causal Refusal Zones ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>): on localized models we constrain DDO layers to start at or before the causal zone; on distributed models the search is unconstrained.</p>
</div>

<td id="A6.T13.2.5.8" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center"><span id="A6.T13.2.5.8.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">1</span></td></tr>
