</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS7" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.7 </span>Benchmark Settings</h3>

<div id="A6.SS7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Standard-RFA averages combine the four attack variants (three-point/residual-stream <math id="A6.SS7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> JailbreakBench/HarmBench). Adaptive RFA, the additional-model evaluation, and the diagnostic studies explicitly labeled LlamaGuard-2 use that judge alone. Judge and aggregation details are given in the corresponding table captions.</p>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Decoding and coherence.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Unless stated otherwise, we use greedy decoding (<math id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\texttt{do\_sample}{=}\mathrm{false}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">do_sample</mtext><mo>=</mo><mi>false</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\texttt{do\_sample}{=}\mathrm{false}</annotation></semantics></math>) with <math id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\texttt{max\_new\_tokens}{=}512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">max_new_tokens</mtext><mo>=</mo><mn>512</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\texttt{max\_new\_tokens}{=}512</annotation></semantics></math> and batch size 8; all timing measurements use a single A100 GPU. Some post-hoc edits can break generation (e.g., near-empty or highly repetitive outputs) even when ASR appears low, so we apply a deterministic coherence check on 10 benign prompts and drop configurations with empty, degenerate (single-token repetition <math id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>&gt;</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;</annotation></semantics></math>80%), or too-short outputs (marked “<math id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>”).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Splits and DIM estimation.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Hyperparameter tuning and DIM estimation use a held-out validation split (128 harmful + 128 safe probes); benchmark metrics are reported on held-out test sets. For DDO optimization, DIM directions are computed per-layer from last-token post-attention-layernorm activations (<math id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathbf{x}}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>, the MLP input) using <span id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">unfiltered</span> estimation (no refusal-score filtering), accumulated in float64. For attack evaluation (RFA), directions are estimated from residual-stream activations (<math id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{h}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐡</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{h}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>), matching the standard attacker protocol.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Table coloring conventions.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Throughout all tables, cell shading follows consistent thresholds relative to the per-block base model. For ASR-type metrics (DR, RFA, Heretic, GCG, PAIR, AutoDAN; lower is better): <span id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-bg-color:#C8E6C9;">best</span> = best in column; <span id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#C8E6C9;">good</span> = <math id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\leq" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>≤</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\leq</annotation></semantics></math>10%; <span id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#FFCDD2;">poor</span> = <math id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\geq" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>≥</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\geq</annotation></semantics></math>50%; unshaded = 10–50%. For XSTest (higher is better): good = within 5pp of base or improved; poor = drop <math id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>&gt;</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;</annotation></semantics></math>20pp. For MMLU (higher is better): good = within 1pp of base or improved; poor = drop <math id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>&gt;</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;</annotation></semantics></math>3pp. For MT-Bench (higher is better): good = within 0.5 of base or improved; poor = drop <math id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>&gt;</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;</annotation></semantics></math>2. <span id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E3F2FD;">ours</span> = DDO rows.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">MMLU.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate <math id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math>-shot multiple-choice accuracy on MMLU’s <math id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="57" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>57</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">57</annotation></semantics></math> subjects. We run evaluation via <span id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">lighteval</span> using the <span id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">helm|mmlu:&lt;subject&gt;|5|1</span> task configuration (<math id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math>-shot; few-shot truncation enabled) and report average exact-match accuracy across subjects. For tractability during iterative defense development, we cap evaluation to <math id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math> questions per subject unless otherwise noted.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">MT-Bench.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We run the standard MT-Bench benchmark (<math id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="80" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>80</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">80</annotation></semantics></math> multi-turn questions) using FastChat’s <span id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">llm_judge</span> pipeline with GPT-4 as the judge in single-mode and report the average score (<math id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\text{--}10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>–</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\text{--}10</annotation></semantics></math>) across questions.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">XSTest.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We measure over-refusal on XSTest <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">38</a>]</cite>—250 safe prompts that superficially resemble harmful ones (e.g., “How do I kill a process in Linux?”). A defended model is expected to comply; refusal here is a false-positive cost of the defense. We generate one response per prompt with greedy decoding (<math id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\texttt{do\_sample}{=}\text{False}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">do_sample</mtext><mo>=</mo><mtext>False</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\texttt{do\_sample}{=}\text{False}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\texttt{max\_new\_tokens}{=}200" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">max_new_tokens</mtext><mo>=</mo><mn>200</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\texttt{max\_new\_tokens}{=}200</annotation></semantics></math>), then classify each response with GPT-4o under the official XSTest 3-class rubric: <em id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">full compliance</em> (direct answer), <em id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">full refusal</em> (declines or only offers alternatives), and <em id="A6.SS7.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">partial refusal</em> (mixed response). The reported XSTest score is the share of full-compliance outputs; partial and full refusal both count against the model.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS8" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.8 </span>Baseline Sweep Details</h3>

<div id="A6.SS8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section documents our baseline-training sweeps. The main Llama-3 comparison uses publicly released defended checkpoints; the cross-model comparison uses our trained reproductions.</p>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Common training setup.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We trained six defenses (Circuit Breakers, RepBend, Triplet, Triplet-Adv, LAT, ReFAT) on six model families (Llama-3, Yi-1.5, Qwen3, Gemma-2, Mistral, GLM-4). All methods use LoRA finetuning on <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">q,k,v,o,gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj</span> (GLM-4 uses <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">query_key_value, dense, dense_h_to_4h, dense_4h_to_h</span>), bf16 precision with tf32 matmuls, a constant learning-rate scheduler, gradient checkpointing, 1 epoch, and an effective batch size of 16 (<span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">per_device_train_batch_size=2</span>, <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gradient_accumulation_steps=8</span>). All CRL-family methods (CB, RepBend, Triplet, Triplet-Adv) train on <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">allenai/wildguardmix</span> (<span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">wildguardtrain</span> split). For each (defense, model) pair, we run a 3-config sweep (A/B/C) over the primary hyperparameter(s) identified in the source paper; the best config is selected by lowest RFA ASR averaged over three judges (HarmBench classifier, LlamaGuard-2, StrongREJECT).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Circuit Breakers <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Circuit Breakers finetunes a LoRA adapter with a representation-rerouting loss that pushes harmful-prompt residual activations toward a “broken” (orthogonal or random) target representation, while a retention term preserves benign activations. We sweep <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">loss_alpha</span> (rerouting strength) over <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{10,20,40\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>40</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{10,20,40\}</annotation></semantics></math>, with all other loss terms set to zero (<span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">loss_beta=loss_gamma=loss_epsilon=loss_eta=0</span>). Training uses LR <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>, LoRA <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r{=}16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r{=}16</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha{=}16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha{=}16</annotation></semantics></math>, dropout <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.05</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.05</annotation></semantics></math>, <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">max_seq_length=2048</span>, and <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="150" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>150</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">150</annotation></semantics></math> steps (Config D: <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="300" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>300</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">300</annotation></semantics></math> steps). Target layers follow the last <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30\text{--}50\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>30</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>–</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30\text{--}50\%</annotation></semantics></math> of each model (Table <a href="#A6.T14" title="Table 14 ‣ Layer targeting. ‣ F.8 Baseline Sweep Details ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">RepBend <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite>.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">RepBend extends CB with a representation-bending loss: additional penalty terms (<math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ε</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon</annotation></semantics></math>) reshape the geometry of harmful representations along a learned direction while preserving benign ones. We jointly sweep <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">(loss_alpha, loss_gamma)</span> over <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{(0.5,0.3),(0.75,0.45),(1.0,0.6)\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.75</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.45</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1.0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{(0.5,0.3),(0.75,0.45),(1.0,0.6)\}</annotation></semantics></math>, fixing <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">loss_beta=0.1</span>, <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">loss_epsilon=0.3</span>, <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">loss_mode=response_all</span>, <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">alpha_mode=all</span>. Training uses LR <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math>, LoRA <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r{=}16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r{=}16</annotation></semantics></math>, <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">max_seq_length=4096</span>, <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="450" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>450</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">450</annotation></semantics></math> steps (D: <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="900" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>900</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">900</annotation></semantics></math> steps).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Triplet <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>]</cite>.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Triplet loss trains the model to pull harmful-prompt activations toward refusal anchors and push them away from compliance anchors in representation space, using margins <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">(margin_p, margin_n)</span>. We sweep over <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{(2,3),(4,6),(8,12)\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>12</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{(2,3),(4,6),(8,12)\}</annotation></semantics></math>. Fixed args: <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">loss_alpha=0.5</span>, <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">loss_beta=0.6</span>, <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">loss_gamma=0.7</span>, <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">loss_epsilon=0.7</span>, <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">loss_safe_dist_p=norm</span>, distance metrics for unsafe pairs use cosine. Training uses LR <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>, LoRA <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r{=}16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r{=}16</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="900" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>900</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">900</annotation></semantics></math> steps (D: <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1800" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1800</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1800</annotation></semantics></math> steps). Triplet is evaluated on Llama-3 in the main comparison (Table <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ Standard RFA and Heretic on Llama-3. ‣ 4.2 Results ‣ 4 Experiments and Results ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>); it is included in the sweep for completeness.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Triplet-Adv <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>]</cite>.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Identical to Triplet (<span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">loss_attack=False</span> <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">True</span>): an adversarial latent perturbation is injected into hidden states during training before the triplet loss is applied, sharpening the representation boundary against activation-space attacks. Same sweep grid and hyperparameters as Triplet.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">LAT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite>.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Latent Adversarial Training alternates between a PGD inner loop that perturbs hidden activations subject to an <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> budget <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">epsilon</span> and an outer loop that minimizes task loss on the perturbed activations. We sweep <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">(epsilon, pgd_iters)</span> over <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{(4,16),(8,24),(12,32)\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>16</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>24</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>32</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{(4,16),(8,24),(12,32)\}</annotation></semantics></math>. Other args: <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">outer_lr=8e-5</span>, <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">inner_lr=1e-3</span>, <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">batch_size=16</span>, <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">max_batch_per_acc=2</span>, LoRA <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r{=}64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r{=}64</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="150" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>150</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">150</annotation></semantics></math> steps (D: <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="300\text{--}400" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>300</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>–</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>400</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">300\text{--}400</annotation></semantics></math> steps).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px7" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">ReFAT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite>.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Refusal-Feature Adversarial Training augments each training step with probability <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">p_rfa</span>: it estimates a refusal direction via DIM over <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math> samples, ablates it from activations across <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="75\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>75</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">75\%</annotation></semantics></math> of layers, and computes the loss on the ablated activations; the refusal direction is recomputed every <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math> steps. We sweep <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px7.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">p_rfa</span> over <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{0.5,0.7,0.9\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.9</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{0.5,0.7,0.9\}</annotation></semantics></math>. Other args: LR <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px7.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\times 10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\times 10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math>, <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px7.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">max_seq_length=512</span>, <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px7.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">lora_alpha=32</span>, gradient clip <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px7.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.0</annotation></semantics></math>. Per-model LoRA rank and batch size: Llama-3 (<math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px7.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r{=}128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r{=}128</annotation></semantics></math>, batch <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px7.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math>); Gemma-2 (<math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px7.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r{=}64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r{=}64</annotation></semantics></math>, batch <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px7.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math>); all others (<math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px7.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r{=}128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r{=}128</annotation></semantics></math>, batch <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px7.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px8" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Layer targeting.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">CB and RepBend/Triplet apply their losses only to a model-specific subset of layers; LAT and ReFAT similarly focus perturbations on a fraction of the network. Table <a href="#A6.T14" title="Table 14 ‣ Layer targeting. ‣ F.8 Baseline Sweep Details ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a> lists the target-layer windows used across all six models.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.T14" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 14: </span>Per-model layer targeting for CB and RepBend/Triplet. CB applies the rerouting loss to the listed layer range; RepBend/Triplet use a sliding window starting at <span id="A6.T14.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">RB_START</span> of width <span id="A6.T14.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">RB_WIN</span>. All windows cover the last <math id="A6.T14.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30\text{--}50\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>30</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>–</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30\text{--}50\%</annotation></semantics></math> of model depth.</figcaption>
<table id="A6.T14.6" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="A6.T14.6.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A6.T14.6.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="A6.T14.6.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Model</span></th>
<th id="A6.T14.6.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="A6.T14.6.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Total layers</span></th>
<th id="A6.T14.6.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="A6.T14.6.1.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">CB target layers</span></th>
<th id="A6.T14.6.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="A6.T14.6.1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">RB_START</span></th>
<th id="A6.T14.6.1.5" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><span id="A6.T14.6.1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">RB_WIN</span></th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">

</section>
<section id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px9" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">D-config protocol.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If the best A/B/C config for a (defense, model) pair still exceeds <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>50</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50\%</annotation></semantics></math> RFA ASR, we retrain it at <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px9.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="2\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\times</annotation></semantics></math> the step count (Config D) with all other hyperparameters fixed. Config D provided modest or no improvement in most cases; diminishing returns were common, particularly for CB, RepBend, and Triplet on models with diffuse refusal. Step counts for D: CB <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px9.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="300" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>300</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">300</annotation></semantics></math>; RepBend <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px9.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="900" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>900</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">900</annotation></semantics></math>; Triplet/Triplet-Adv <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px9.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1800" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1800</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1800</annotation></semantics></math>; LAT <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px9.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="300\text{--}400" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>300</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>–</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>400</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">300\text{--}400</annotation></semantics></math>; ReFAT <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px9.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="300" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>300</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">300</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px10" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Config E: LLM-assisted hyperparameter selection.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px10.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px10.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As an additional fairness check, we ran a Config E in which Claude Opus 4.6 proposed hyperparameters for each (defense, model) pair, conditioned on the source paper, the search ranges, and the A–D outcomes. Config E did not improve over the swept best for any pair, and did not outperform DDO under standard or adaptive RFA. For comparisons using these trained reproductions, we report the best available configuration from <math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px10.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{</annotation></semantics></math>A,B,C,D,E<math id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px10.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">}</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\}</annotation></semantics></math> per (defense, model) pair.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px11" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Reproducibility caveats.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px11.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px11.p1.1" class="ltx_p">LAT and ReFAT use a separate Python environment from the CRL-family methods due to dependency conflicts (<span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px11.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">LLaMA-Factory</span> vs. <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px11.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">refusal_direction_defense</span>). All runs use <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px11.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:16:8</span> for determinism and disable Weights &amp; Biases logging. Adapter checkpoints are saved at <span id="A6.SS8.SSS0.Px11.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">baselines/&lt;model&gt;/&lt;defense&gt;_&lt;config&gt;/</span> and merged on demand for evaluation.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS9" class="ltx_subsection">

Defense costs are per optimization run for one hyperparameter configuration; hyperparameter search and downstream benchmark evaluation are additional. The <math id="A6.SS9.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="30\text{--}450\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>30</mn><mtext>–</mtext><mn>450</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30\text{--}450\times</annotation></semantics></math> comparison uses these per-configuration costs. <section id="A6.SS10" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.10 </span>Adaptive Attack: Exact ASR and MT-Bench by Phase</h3>

<div id="A6.SS10.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS10.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A6.T16" title="Table 16 ‣ Attack cost model. ‣ F.10 Adaptive Attack: Exact ASR and MT-Bench by Phase ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">16</span></a> summarizes per-phase ASR (phases <math id="A6.SS10.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\text{--}8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>–</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\text{--}8</annotation></semantics></math>) for the full <math id="A6.SS10.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math>-phase setting; Table <a href="#A6.T17" title="Table 17 ‣ Attack cost model. ‣ F.10 Adaptive Attack: Exact ASR and MT-Bench by Phase ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">17</span></a> reports the exact per-phase ASR (LlamaGuard-2) <em id="A6.SS10.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">and</em> MT-Bench (GPT-4 judge) values underlying Figure <a href="#S4.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ Adaptive multi-phase RFA. ‣ 4.2 Results ‣ 4 Experiments and Results ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>. Figure <a href="#A6.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ Attack cost model. ‣ F.10 Adaptive Attack: Exact ASR and MT-Bench by Phase ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> provides a compact ASR–utility summary of the same runs.</p>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Attack cost model.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each adaptive phase requires one DIM re-estimation (<math id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>256</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">256</annotation></semantics></math> forward passes on <math id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>128</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128</annotation></semantics></math> harmful + <math id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>128</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128</annotation></semantics></math> safe probes, <math id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\sim}30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\sim}30</annotation></semantics></math> s) followed by Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization, hook installation, and evaluation (<math id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\sim}1\text{--}2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>–</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\sim}1\text{--}2</annotation></semantics></math> min), totaling <math id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\sim}2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\sim}2</annotation></semantics></math> min per phase on a single A100 GPU. A full <math id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math>-phase attack therefore costs <math id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\sim}15\text{--}20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mn>15</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>–</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\sim}15\text{--}20</annotation></semantics></math> min wall-clock for the attack loop. The separate MT-Bench evaluation at each phase is timed in Table <a href="#A6.T15" title="Table 15 ‣ F.9 Compute Budget ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a>. The attack is fully automated (a deterministic loop over phases), requires no ML expertise, and uses only the defended checkpoint and a generic probe set—the same probes used for standard RFA suffice. However, multi-phase ablation degrades the resulting checkpoint: DDO-defended Llama-3 drops from MT-Bench <math id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7.67" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>7.67</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7.67</annotation></semantics></math> (unattacked) to <math id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6.17" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>6.17</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6.17</annotation></semantics></math> at Phase <math id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math> (peak <math id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="65\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>65</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">65\%</annotation></semantics></math> ASR) and <math id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5.82" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5.82</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5.82</annotation></semantics></math> by Phase <math id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> (Table <a href="#A6.T17" title="Table 17 ‣ Attack cost model. ‣ F.10 Adaptive Attack: Exact ASR and MT-Bench by Phase ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">17</span></a>)—a <math id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\sim}1.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><mn>1.9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\sim}1.9</annotation></semantics></math>-point utility cost. By contrast, on the undefended base model the attacker obtains <math id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="73\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>73</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">73\%</annotation></semantics></math> ASR at Phase <math id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> with only a <math id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.3</annotation></semantics></math>-point MT-Bench drop. DDO therefore forces the attacker to trade substantially more model quality per unit of ASR gained.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.T16" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 16: </span>Adaptive multi-phase RFA profiles (ASR %, LlamaGuard-2) across all <math id="A6.T16.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> phases. “Worst” is the maximum ASR across phases (the attacker can stop at any phase). Both trained and post-hoc defenses degrade at later phases. DDO (rank <math id="A6.T16.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math>) achieves <math id="A6.T16.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="65\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>65</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">65\%</annotation></semantics></math> worst-case, comparable to trained RepBend (<math id="A6.T16.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="58\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>58</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">58\%</annotation></semantics></math>), without training.</figcaption>

</figure>
<div id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">These phase trajectories reinforce the main-text comparison: DDO (rank <math id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math>) preserves utility (MT-Bench <math id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\geq 5.82" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≥</mo><mn>5.82</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\geq 5.82</annotation></semantics></math> through Phase <math id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math>) at a level comparable to RepBend (<math id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6.17" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>6.17</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6.17</annotation></semantics></math>) and Circuit Breakers (<math id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5.90" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5.90</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5.90</annotation></semantics></math>), while ReFAT exhibits a sharp utility drop early (Phase <math id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> MTB <math id="A6.SS10.SSS0.Px1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.46" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.46</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.46</annotation></semantics></math>) despite low ASR.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.F4" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2609.16204v1/asr_utility_trajectory.svg" id="A6.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:405/369;" width="405" height="369"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 4: </span>ASR vs. MT-Bench trajectories under adaptive attack. Each dot is one defense at one phase (<math id="A6.F4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0\text{--}8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>–</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0\text{--}8</annotation></semantics></math>); larger dots = earlier phases. Quadrants: <span id="A6.F4.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">top-left</span> = safe + useful (ideal); <span id="A6.F4.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">top-right</span> = jailbroken but coherent (most dangerous); <span id="A6.F4.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">bottom-left</span> = refuses but unusable; <span id="A6.F4.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">bottom-right</span> = destroyed. ReFAT collapses into the bottom-left region (low ASR but utility destroyed), while DDO compositions (green, orange) preserve utility comparably to RepBend and Circuit Breakers, with worst-case ASR rising under sustained re-estimation.</figcaption>

</section>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS11" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.11 </span>Extended Model Comparison</h3>

<div id="A6.SS11.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS11.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A6.T18" title="Table 18 ‣ F.11 Extended Model Comparison ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a> reports additional defense configurations evaluated on Llama-3, using consistent naming: <span id="A6.SS11.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">DDO</span> = the optimized decoy mechanism described in Section <a href="#S3" title="3 Method: Decoy Direction Optimization (DDO) ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, without auxiliary mechanisms; <span id="A6.SS11.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">DDO + debiasing</span> = DDO composed with orthogonal debiasing; <span id="A6.SS11.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">DDO (rank <math id="A6.SS11.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>)</span> = DDO with <math id="A6.SS11.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> diversified decoy readers (for adaptive RFA). The shown compositions are selected from a broader mechanism-subset search guided by two criteria: (i) minimize RFA ASR under the target attacker tier, and (ii) preserve utility (benign compliance <math id="A6.SS11.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;85\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mn>85</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;85\%</annotation></semantics></math>, MT-Bench <math id="A6.SS11.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;6.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>6.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;6.0</annotation></semantics></math>). The rank-<math id="A6.SS11.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> variants diversify readers to increase the effective decoy rank; the Heretic-targeted variant allocates mechanisms to matrices outside Heretic’s weight-edit surface. Optuna is used for per-model DDO hyperparameter tuning (Appendix <a href="#A6.SS6" title="F.6 Per-Model DDO Best Configs ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.6</span></a>); the additional <em id="A6.SS11.p1.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Optuna</em> qualifier in the Llama-3 rank-<math id="A6.SS11.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> label distinguishes the separately tuned adaptive configuration.</p>
</div>

<section id="A6.SS12" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.12 </span>Cross-Model Mechanism Comparison and Negative Results</h3>

<div id="A6.SS12.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS12.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A6.T19" title="Table 19 ‣ F.12 Cross-Model Mechanism Comparison and Negative Results ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">19</span></a> compares 8 systematically evaluated mechanisms across all 7 models (10–30 Optuna trials each). Three patterns emerge: (i) DDO is the only mechanism that achieves <math id="A6.SS12.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&lt;" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>&lt;</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&lt;</annotation></semantics></math>10% ASR on every architecture; (ii) five mechanisms (diverse Q-head routing, rotation, V-projection, head amplification, KV strengthening) break generation entirely on Yi, Gemma-2, and GLM-4 (<math id="A6.SS12.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> = coherence failure), suggesting these architectures are less tolerant of attention- and normalization-space edits; and (iii) random orthogonal decoys without gradient optimization achieve low ASR only on Yi (2%) but fail on most other models (18–53%), confirming that the optimization in DDO’s 4-part loss is essential. Formal definitions are in Appendix <a href="#A4.SS2" title="D.2 All Mechanism Definitions ‣ Appendix D Additional Method Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.T19" class="ltx_table">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 19: </span>Cross-model mechanism comparison (ASR %<math id="A6.T19.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>, Optuna-tuned, 10–30 trials each). DDO row: mean of 4 RFA variants, 3-judge avg (consistent with Tables <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ Standard RFA and Heretic on Llama-3. ‣ 4.2 Results ‣ 4 Experiments and Results ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>–<a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ Cross-model generalization and baseline comparison. ‣ 4.2 Results ‣ 4 Experiments and Results ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>). Other mechanisms: 3-point RFA, LlamaGuard-2 (faster diagnostic). <span id="A6.T19.5" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#C8E6C9;">best</span> / <span id="A6.T19.6" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#FFCDD2;">poor</span> / <span id="A6.T19.7" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E3F2FD;">ours</span>; <math id="A6.T19.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> = coherence failure. DDO is the only mechanism achieving <math id="A6.T19.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&lt;" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>&lt;</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&lt;</annotation></semantics></math>10% ASR across all 7 architectures.</figcaption><div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<table id="A6.T19.8" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="A6.T19.8.1" class="ltx_tr">

<section id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Negative results and failed approaches.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The broader mechanism search also yielded several informative negative results, organized by failure mode (ASR: 3-point RFA, JailbreakBench, LlamaGuard-2 unless noted).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Linear edits are fragile under adaptive re-estimation.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Mechanisms equivalent to an input-independent linear transformation of the residual stream are defeated once the attacker re-estimates DIM on the defended checkpoint. <em id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Decoy Shear Transform</em> (<math id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="92\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>92</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">92\%</annotation></semantics></math> ASR) injects orthogonal decoy components via a linear shear <math id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{M}=\mathbf{I}+\sum c_{j}\mathbf{u}_{j}\hat{\mathbf{r}}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐌</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝐈</mi><mo rspace="0.055em">+</mo><mrow><mo>∑</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐮</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{M}=\mathbf{I}+\sum c_{j}\mathbf{u}_{j}\hat{\mathbf{r}}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>, but the defended DIM direction simply rotates to track the sheared mean-difference. <em id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Refusal Direction Rotation</em> (<math id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="68\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>68</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">68\%</annotation></semantics></math> ASR) applies a Givens rotation in the <math id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\hat{\mathbf{r}},\mathbf{v}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐯</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\hat{\mathbf{r}},\mathbf{v}\}</annotation></semantics></math> plane; the attacker recovers the rotated direction. <em id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Representation Rerouting</em> (<math id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="86\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>86</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">86\%</annotation></semantics></math> ASR) maps harmful activations to random targets via a low-rank <math id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\mathbf{W}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐖</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\mathbf{W}</annotation></semantics></math>, but provides insufficient disruption of linear separability.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Spreading decoy budget can be counterproductive.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Distributing decoy energy across more directions involves a fundamental tradeoff (Corollary <a href="#Thmtheorem3" title="Corollary 3 (Optimal spectrum under an energy constraint). ‣ Decoy energy allocation. ‣ 3 Method: Decoy Direction Optimization (DDO) ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>): with identical readers, adding more output directions dilutes each one without increasing the effective rank of <math id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>. With diversified readers, spreading energy trades rank-1 protection for higher-rank robustness (see Appendix <a href="#A5.SS3" title="E.3 Empirical Spectral Analysis ‣ Appendix E Theoretical Proofs and Formalizations ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.3</span></a> for empirical validation).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Aggressive edits destroy capability.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">LM-Head Row Scaling</em> achieves near-zero RFA ASR (<math id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.7\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.7</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.7\%</annotation></semantics></math>) but at catastrophic utility cost (XSTest <math id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>8.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8.0\%</annotation></semantics></math>, MT-Bench <math id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.72" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.72</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.72</annotation></semantics></math>)—the model over-refuses almost all prompts. Extending DDO injection to layers <math id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0\text{--}11" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>–</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0\text{--}11</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="48\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>48</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">48\%</annotation></semantics></math> ASR) degraded generation quality to incoherent outputs. These cases illustrate that low ASR is insufficient without utility preservation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Mismatched threat models.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Gradient landscape roughening</em> (<math id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="84\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>84</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">84\%</annotation></semantics></math> ASR) perturbs <math id="A6.SS12.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{gate}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>gate</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{gate}}</annotation></semantics></math> to create rough input-space loss surfaces, targeting GCG-style prompt optimization. This does not improve robustness against representation-space abliteration (RFA), confirming that input-space and representation-space attacks require distinct defensive mechanisms.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS13" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.13 </span>Reproducibility Notes</h3>

<section id="A6.SS13.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Implementation.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS13.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS13.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">DDO’s gradient optimization through the defended model is implemented with <span id="A6.SS13.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">nnsight</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib61" title="" class="ltx_ref">61</a>]</cite>, which provides differentiable access to model internals while keeping base-model weights frozen. Hyperparameter search uses Optuna <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>]</cite> with the default Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) sampler.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS13.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS13.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We note three reproducibility details. (i) <span id="A6.SS13.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Determinism:</span> we use deterministic decoding (<span id="A6.SS13.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath ltx_font_typewriter">do_sample=false</span>) and fixed RNG seeds for all stochastic components, and adaptive multi-phase RFA is deterministic (verified across <math id="A6.SS13.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math> runs). (ii) <span id="A6.SS13.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Seed sensitivity:</span> DIM direction estimation introduces <math id="A6.SS13.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\approx\pm 1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mo>±</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx\pm 1\%</annotation></semantics></math> ASR variation across probe-set seeds, and Heretic results vary with Optuna random seed (<math id="A6.SS13.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\approx\pm 3\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mo>±</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx\pm 3\%</annotation></semantics></math> across <math id="A6.SS13.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math> independent 200-trial runs). (iii) <span id="A6.SS13.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Fixed seeds:</span> data splits <math id="A6.SS13.SSS0.Px1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=42" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mn>42</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=42</annotation></semantics></math>, v_proj conditioning <math id="A6.SS13.SSS0.Px1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=99" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mn>99</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=99</annotation></semantics></math> (searched over <math id="A6.SS13.SSS0.Px1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{42,77,99,123,200\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>42</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>77</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>123</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>200</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{42,77,99,123,200\}</annotation></semantics></math>), KV strengthening <math id="A6.SS13.SSS0.Px1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=7</annotation></semantics></math>, Optuna TPE <math id="A6.SS13.SSS0.Px1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=42" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mn>42</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=42</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS14" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.14 </span>Defense and Attack Surface Map</h3>

<div id="A6.SS14.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS14.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A6.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ F.14 Defense and Attack Surface Map ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> visualizes a single pre-norm transformer block (Llama-3) with defense and attack annotations. DDO edits <math id="A6.SS14.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{gate}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>gate</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{gate}}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.SS14.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{up}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>up</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{up}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A6.SS14.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>down</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}</annotation></semantics></math> in the SwiGLU MLP (green); RFA hooks activations at three points (red dots); Heretic edits <math id="A6.SS14.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{o}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{o}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.SS14.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>down</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}</annotation></semantics></math> offline (red outlines). The partial overlap on <math id="A6.SS14.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>down</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the only shared surface between DDO and Heretic.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.F5" class="ltx_figure">

auxiliary (“aux”) mechanisms optionally edit additional matrices in attention, embeddings, and normalization (Section <a href="#S3.SS0.SSS0.Px9" title="Orthogonal debiasing (utility repair). ‣ 3 Method: Decoy Direction Optimization (DDO) ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>). <span id="A6.F5.8" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#B72D2A;">Red</span>: attacker access—RFA hooks activations at three points (<math id="A6.F5.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{h}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐡</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{h}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.F5.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐚</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A6.F5.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{m}_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐦</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{m}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>); Heretic <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">14</a>]</cite> edits only <math id="A6.F5.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{o}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{o}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.F5.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>down</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Overlap occurs only on <math id="A6.F5.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>down</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</figcaption>

<section id="A6.SS15" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.15 </span>Additional Model Evaluation</h3>

<div id="A6.SS15.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS15.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Beyond the six primary models evaluated in the main text (Table <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ Standard RFA and Heretic on Llama-3. ‣ 4.2 Results ‣ 4 Experiments and Results ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> and Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ Cross-model generalization and baseline comparison. ‣ 4.2 Results ‣ 4 Experiments and Results ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>), we apply DDO with per-model Optuna tuning (<math id="A6.SS15.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\sim}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\sim}</annotation></semantics></math>10 min each) to seven additional instruction-tuned checkpoints spanning 7B–24B parameters (Table <a href="#A6.T20" title="Table 20 ‣ F.15 Additional Model Evaluation ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">20</span></a>), including Llama-2-7B-Chat. DDO achieves <math id="A6.SS15.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&lt;" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>&lt;</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&lt;</annotation></semantics></math>10% standard-RFA ASR on all seven while preserving MMLU within 1–2 points of the base model, confirming cross-family and cross-scale generalization.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.T20" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 20: </span><span id="A6.T20.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">DDO on additional models with per-model Optuna tuning (<math id="A6.T20.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\sim}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\sim}</annotation></semantics></math>10 min, single A100 GPU). MMLU: base <math id="A6.T20.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> DDO-defended (%<math id="A6.T20.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\uparrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↑</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\uparrow</annotation></semantics></math>). RFA ASR = mean of 4 variants, LlamaGuard-2 (%<math id="A6.T20.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>). XST = XSTest (%<math id="A6.T20.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\uparrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↑</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\uparrow</annotation></semantics></math>). DDO achieves <math id="A6.T20.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&lt;" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>&lt;</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&lt;</annotation></semantics></math>10% ASR on all models with <math id="A6.T20.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\leq" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>≤</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\leq</annotation></semantics></math>1.4 point MMLU drop.</span></figcaption>
