<section id="A6.SS16" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.16 </span>DDO Undo Attack Analysis</h3>

<div id="A6.SS16.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS16.p1.1" class="ltx_p">An attacker who obtains only the defended checkpoint (without the original base model) might attempt to identify and revert DDO-modified neurons. A natural undo heuristic is to score each MLP gate row by its projection onto the attacker’s estimated refusal direction, <math id="A6.SS16.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{i}\mathrel{\triangleq}\left|\mathbf{w}_{\mathrm{gate}}^{(i)}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\mathrm{atk}}\right|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐰</mi><mi>gate</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐝</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>atk</mi></msub></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{i}\mathrel{\triangleq}\left|\mathbf{w}_{\mathrm{gate}}^{(i)}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\mathrm{atk}}\right|</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A6.SS16.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\mathrm{atk}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐝</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>atk</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\mathrm{atk}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the DIM direction estimated on the defended checkpoint, and then zero the top-scoring neurons. DDO’s gate rows are shaped to align with the reference refusal direction <math id="A6.SS16.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\mathrm{clean}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>clean</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\mathrm{clean}}</annotation></semantics></math> (so the trigger fires on harmful inputs), which would make them easy to find—if <math id="A6.SS16.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\mathrm{atk}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐝</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>atk</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\mathrm{atk}}</annotation></semantics></math> matched <math id="A6.SS16.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\mathrm{clean}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>clean</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\mathrm{clean}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Estimator corruption rotates <math id="A6.SS16.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\mathrm{atk}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐝</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>atk</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\mathrm{atk}}</annotation></semantics></math> away from <math id="A6.SS16.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\mathrm{clean}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>clean</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\mathrm{clean}}</annotation></semantics></math>, frustrating this undo strategy.</p>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Detectability in intermediate layers.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Across Qwen3, Mistral-7B, and Yi, DDO target layers in the mid-zone show <math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\cos(\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\mathrm{clean}},\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\mathrm{atk}})\in[-0.05,+0.05]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>clean</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐝</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>atk</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos(\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\mathrm{clean}},\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\mathrm{atk}})\in[-0.05,+0.05]</annotation></semantics></math>, so the estimated directions are nearly orthogonal. The modified row’s projection <math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{\mathrm{mod}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>mod</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{\mathrm{mod}}</annotation></semantics></math> collapses to within the natural top-<math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math> distribution:</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="A6.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A6.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A6.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Qwen3 L14</span>: <math id="A6.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{\mathrm{mod}}=0.267" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>mod</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.267</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{\mathrm{mod}}=0.267</annotation></semantics></math> vs. natural rank-<math id="A6.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A6.I1.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.230" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.230</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.230</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="A6.I1.i1.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.16\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.16</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.16\times</annotation></semantics></math> margin).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A6.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A6.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Mistral-7B L10</span>: <math id="A6.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{\mathrm{mod}}=0.041" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>mod</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.041</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{\mathrm{mod}}=0.041</annotation></semantics></math>, outranked by a natural neuron at <math id="A6.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.066" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.066</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.066</annotation></semantics></math> (rank <math id="A6.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A6.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A6.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Yi L26</span>: <math id="A6.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{\mathrm{mod}}=0.112" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>mod</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.112</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{\mathrm{mod}}=0.112</annotation></semantics></math> vs. natural rank-<math id="A6.I1.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A6.I1.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.075" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.075</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.075</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="A6.I1.i3.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.48\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.48</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.48\times</annotation></semantics></math> margin).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A6.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A6.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Yi L32</span>: <math id="A6.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{\mathrm{mod}}=0.095" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>mod</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.095</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{\mathrm{mod}}=0.095</annotation></semantics></math> vs. natural rank-<math id="A6.I1.i4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A6.I1.i4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.091" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.091</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.091</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="A6.I1.i4.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1.04\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.04</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.04\times</annotation></semantics></math> margin).</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Instruction-tuned models naturally contain MLP neurons whose gate rows align with refusal at the <math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.07\text{--}0.20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.07</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>–</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>0.20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.07\text{--}0.20</annotation></semantics></math> level—these are real refusal-relevant neurons doing work in the model’s native safety circuitry. Once <math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\mathrm{atk}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐝</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>atk</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\mathrm{atk}}</annotation></semantics></math> has been rotated away from <math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\mathrm{clean}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>clean</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\mathrm{clean}}</annotation></semantics></math>, DDO’s modified neuron sits inside this distribution rather than as an outlier. The undo attack scores neurons using this corrupted direction estimate. In the Llama-3 evaluation, it provides partial recovery while remaining below the undefended ASR (Table <a href="#A6.T21" title="Table 21 ‣ Post-attack ASR under undo heuristics. ‣ F.16 DDO Undo Attack Analysis ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">21</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Detectability in later layers.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">At the deepest target layers, deception can be slightly weaker. Yi L37 (the deepest layer in Yi’s L14–37 zone) shows <math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\cos(\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\mathrm{clean}},\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\mathrm{atk}})\approx 0.09" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>clean</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐝</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>atk</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.09</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos(\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{\mathrm{clean}},\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\mathrm{atk}})\approx 0.09</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{\mathrm{mod}}=0.444" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>mod</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.444</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{\mathrm{mod}}=0.444</annotation></semantics></math> exceeds the natural rank-<math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.081" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.081</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.081</annotation></semantics></math>) by <math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="{\sim}5\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>∼</mo><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\sim}5\times</annotation></semantics></math>. However, since the attacker must search the full model without knowing which layers were modified, even a partial margin at one layer does not yield reliable undo across the model. Placing DDO inside the model’s natural causal refusal zone gives the defense a stealth property: the modification shares its surface signature with the neurons it is functionally hiding among.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Post-attack ASR under undo heuristics.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To complement the geometric analysis above, we measure post-attack ASR after applying each undo heuristic followed by standard RFA. For each heuristic, we zero the top-<math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> down-projection columns per DDO layer, then run 3-point RFA (Table <a href="#A6.T21" title="Table 21 ‣ Post-attack ASR under undo heuristics. ‣ F.16 DDO Undo Attack Analysis ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">21</span></a>).</p>
</div>

<td id="A6.T21.4.2.7" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_t"><span id="A6.T21.4.2.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">13</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A6.T21.4.3" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.T21.4.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left"><span id="A6.T21.4.3.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">gate/up cosine</span></td>
<td id="A6.T21.4.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="A6.T21.4.3.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">17</span></td>
<td id="A6.T21.4.3.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="A6.T21.4.3.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">14</span></td>
<td id="A6.T21.4.3.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="A6.T21.4.3.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">16</span></td>
<td id="A6.T21.4.3.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="A6.T21.4.3.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">15</span></td>
<td id="A6.T21.4.3.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="A6.T21.4.3.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">12</span></td>
<td id="A6.T21.4.3.7" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center"><span id="A6.T21.4.3.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">14</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A6.T21.4.4" class="ltx_tr" style="--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">
<td id="A6.T21.4.4.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb"><span id="A6.T21.4.4.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">down-col norm</span></td>
<td id="A6.T21.4.4.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A6.T21.4.4.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">4</span></td>
<td id="A6.T21.4.4.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A6.T21.4.4.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">7</span></td>
<td id="A6.T21.4.4.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A6.T21.4.4.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">5</span></td>
<td id="A6.T21.4.4.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A6.T21.4.4.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">5</span></td>
<td id="A6.T21.4.4.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A6.T21.4.4.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">4</span></td>
<td id="A6.T21.4.4.7" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A6.T21.4.4.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">4</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The gate<math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\cdot\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\mathrm{atk}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐝</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>atk</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cdot\hat{\mathbf{d}}_{\mathrm{atk}}</annotation></semantics></math> and gate/up cosine heuristics yield 12–17% ASR after RFA, indicating partial recovery while remaining below the undefended base (80%). The down-column-norm heuristic yields 4–7% ASR, indicating little recovery under this heuristic. Zeroing a neuron’s down-projection column removes its contribution to the residual stream, including any decoy output from that neuron.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Norm-based detection.</h4>

<div id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A detector could flag DDO neurons by their gate/up norm ratio. In the default compile mode, <math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{w}_{\mathrm{gate}}=\beta\hat{\mathbf{r}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐰</mi><mi>gate</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{w}_{\mathrm{gate}}=\beta\hat{\mathbf{r}}</annotation></semantics></math> (norm <math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math>) and <math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{w}_{\mathrm{up}}=\hat{\mathbf{r}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐰</mi><mi>up</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{w}_{\mathrm{up}}=\hat{\mathbf{r}}</annotation></semantics></math> (norm <math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>), yielding a ratio of <math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta\approx 3\text{--}6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>–</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta\approx 3\text{--}6</annotation></semantics></math>—an outlier among <math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\sim}12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\sim}12</annotation></semantics></math>K neurons. However, this is an artifact of a particular compile choice, not a fundamental limitation. The trigger output depends on the <em id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">product</em> of gate and up norms: <math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{silu}(\mathbf{w}_{\mathrm{gate}}^{\top}\tilde{\mathbf{x}})\cdot\mathbf{w}_{\mathrm{up}}^{\top}\tilde{\mathbf{x}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>silu</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐰</mi><mi>gate</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐰</mi><mi>up</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{silu}(\mathbf{w}_{\mathrm{gate}}^{\top}\tilde{\mathbf{x}})\cdot\mathbf{w}_{\mathrm{up}}^{\top}\tilde{\mathbf{x}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Redistributing the total gain—e.g., setting both to <math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sqrt{\beta}\,\hat{\mathbf{r}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mi>β</mi></msqrt><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{\beta}\,\hat{\mathbf{r}}</annotation></semantics></math>—equalizes norms while preserving the trigger in the large-activation regime (<math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{silu}(x)\approx x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>silu</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{silu}(x)\approx x</annotation></semantics></math>): <math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px4.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{silu}(\sqrt{\beta}\,a)\cdot\sqrt{\beta}\,a\approx\beta a^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>silu</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msqrt><mi>β</mi></msqrt><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msqrt><mi>β</mi></msqrt></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{silu}(\sqrt{\beta}\,a)\cdot\sqrt{\beta}\,a\approx\beta a^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, matching the original. Similarly, <math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px4.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{cossim}(\mathbf{w}_{\mathrm{gate}},\mathbf{w}_{\mathrm{up}})=1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>cossim</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐰</mi><mi>gate</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐰</mi><mi>up</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{cossim}(\mathbf{w}_{\mathrm{gate}},\mathbf{w}_{\mathrm{up}})=1.0</annotation></semantics></math> can be reduced by adding a small orthogonal perturbation <math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px4.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon\,\mathbf{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐯</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon\,\mathbf{v}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px4.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{w}_{\mathrm{up}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐰</mi><mi>up</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{w}_{\mathrm{up}}</annotation></semantics></math>, introducing <math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px4.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\varepsilon)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ε</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O(\varepsilon)</annotation></semantics></math> trigger noise absorbed by the down-projection scale. DDO’s free scalar parameters <math id="A6.SS16.SSS0.Px4.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\beta,s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\beta,s)</annotation></semantics></math> provide the degrees of freedom to match any target norm and cosine distribution analytically. All models evaluated in this paper use the default compile without norm redistribution or cosine camouflage.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS17" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.17 </span>Rank-<math id="A6.SS17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> Attack Sweep</h3>

<div id="A6.SS17.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS17.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To test robustness beyond rank-1 RFA, we evaluate rank-<math id="A6.SS17.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> SVD attacks: the attacker computes the top-<math id="A6.SS17.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> left singular vectors of a harmful–safe contrast matrix on the defended model and ablates all <math id="A6.SS17.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> directions simultaneously (Table <a href="#A6.T22" title="Table 22 ‣ F.17 Rank-𝑘 Attack Sweep ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">22</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.T22" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 22: </span><span id="A6.T22.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Rank-<math id="A6.T22.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> attack sweep on Llama-3-8B DDO (ASR %<math id="A6.T22.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>, LlamaGuard-2, 3-point RFA, JailbreakBench). ASR increases with attack rank in this sweep, reaching 79% at <math id="A6.T22.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k{=}32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k{=}32</annotation></semantics></math>, compared with 80% for the undefended model.</span></figcaption>

<td id="A6.T22.4.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt"><span id="A6.T22.4.1.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">4</span></td>

<div id="A6.SS17.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS17.p2.1" class="ltx_p">ASR increases from 4% at <math id="A6.SS17.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k{=}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k{=}1</annotation></semantics></math> to 29% at <math id="A6.SS17.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k{=}8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k{=}8</annotation></semantics></math> and 39% at <math id="A6.SS17.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k{=}16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k{=}16</annotation></semantics></math>. At <math id="A6.SS17.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k{=}32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k{=}32</annotation></semantics></math>, ASR reaches 79%, approaching the undefended base (80%). These results show decreasing protection against the higher-rank attacks evaluated in this sweep.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS18" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.18 </span>Probe-Budget Sensitivity</h3>

<div id="A6.SS18.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS18.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A natural concern is that DDO’s estimator corruption might rely on the attacker having too few probes for accurate DIM estimation. We test this by varying the attacker’s probe budget from 32 to 1024 prompts in each of the harmful and safe sets (Table <a href="#A6.T23" title="Table 23 ‣ F.18 Probe-Budget Sensitivity ‣ Appendix F Full Experimental Details ‣ Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">23</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.T23" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 23: </span><span id="A6.T23.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Probe-budget sweep on Llama-3-8B DDO (ASR %<math id="A6.T23.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>, LlamaGuard-2, 3-point RFA, JailbreakBench). <math id="A6.T23.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of prompts in each of the harmful and safe sets (<math id="A6.T23.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2N</annotation></semantics></math> prompts total). DDO optimization uses 128 harmful and 128 safe prompts (256 total). ASR ranges from 6% to 12% without a sustained increase over the evaluated budgets.</span></figcaption>
<table id="A6.T23.4" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_align_middle">
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="A6.T23.4.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A6.T23.4.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_tt"><span id="A6.T23.4.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">Prompts per class, <math id="A6.T23.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math></span></td>
<td id="A6.T23.4.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt"><span id="A6.T23.4.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">32</span></td>
<td id="A6.T23.4.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt"><span id="A6.T23.4.1.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">64</span></td>
<td id="A6.T23.4.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt"><span id="A6.T23.4.1.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">128</span></td>
<td id="A6.T23.4.1.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt"><span id="A6.T23.4.1.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">256</span></td>
<td id="A6.T23.4.1.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt"><span id="A6.T23.4.1.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">512</span></td>
<td id="A6.T23.4.1.7" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt"><span id="A6.T23.4.1.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">1024</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A6.T23.4.2" class="ltx_tr" style="--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">
<td id="A6.T23.4.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t"><span id="A6.T23.4.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">ASR (%)</span></td>
<td id="A6.T23.4.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t"><span id="A6.T23.4.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">7</span></td>
<td id="A6.T23.4.2.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t"><span id="A6.T23.4.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">6</span></td>
<td id="A6.T23.4.2.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t"><span id="A6.T23.4.2.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">8</span></td>
<td id="A6.T23.4.2.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t"><span id="A6.T23.4.2.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">12</span></td>
<td id="A6.T23.4.2.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t"><span id="A6.T23.4.2.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">7</span></td>
<td id="A6.T23.4.2.7" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t"><span id="A6.T23.4.2.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#F5F5F5;">7</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="A6.SS18.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS18.p2.1" class="ltx_p">ASR ranges from 6% to 12% as the number of prompts per class increases from 32 to 1024. The 12% result at <math id="A6.SS18.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N{=}256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>256</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N{=}256</annotation></semantics></math> is followed by 7% at both <math id="A6.SS18.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N{=}512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>512</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N{=}512</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A6.SS18.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N{=}1024" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1024</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N{=}1024</annotation></semantics></math>. Even with 1024 prompts per class (8<math id="A6.SS18.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> the DDO optimization budget of 128 per class), the attacker cannot recover the true refusal direction. This confirms that DDO’s defense operates by genuinely corrupting the mean-difference direction, not by exploiting finite-sample noise in the attacker’s estimator.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS19" class="ltx_subsection">

<div id="A6.SS19.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS19.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All models, benchmarks, and software used in this work are publicly available under permissive or research-friendly licenses. We use each asset in accordance with its stated terms.</p>
</div>

      support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the
      methods listed below:</p>
    <ul>
      <li>Click the "Report Issue" <span class="mobile-only">(<svg role="presentation"
            style="display: inline-block; vertical-align: middle; fill: var(--text-color);" aria-hidden="true"
            height="1em" viewBox="0 0 640 640">
            <path
              d="M224 160C224 107 267 64 320 64C373 64 416 107 416 160L416 163.6C416 179.3 403.3 192 387.6 192L252.5 192C236.8 192 224.1 179.3 224.1 163.6L224.1 160zM569.6 172.8C580.2 186.9 577.3 207 563.2 217.6L465.4 290.9C470.7 299.8 474.7 309.6 477.2 320L576 320C593.7 320 608 334.3 608 352C608 369.7 593.7 384 576 384L480 384L480 416C480 418.6 479.9 421.3 479.8 423.9L563.2 486.4C577.3 497 580.2 517.1 569.6 531.2C559 545.3 538.9 548.2 524.8 537.6L461.7 490.3C438.5 534.5 395.2 566.5 344 574.2L344 344C344 330.7 333.3 320 320 320C306.7 320 296 330.7 296 344L296 574.2C244.8 566.5 201.5 534.5 178.3 490.3L115.2 537.6C101.1 548.2 81 545.3 70.4 531.2C59.8 517.1 62.7 497 76.8 486.4L160.2 423.9C160.1 421.3 160 418.7 160 416L160 384L64 384C46.3 384 32 369.7 32 352C32 334.3 46.3 320 64 320L162.8 320C165.3 309.6 169.3 299.8 174.6 290.9L76.8 217.6C62.7 207 59.8 186.9 70.4 172.8C81 158.7 101.1 155.8 115.2 166.4L224 248C236.3 242.9 249.8 240 264 240L376 240C390.2 240 403.7 242.8 416 248L524.8 166.4C538.9 155.8 559 158.7 569.6 172.8z" />
          </svg>)</span> button, located in the page header.</li>
    </ul>
    <p><strong>Tip:</strong> You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.</p>
    <p>Our team has already identified <a class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/arXiv/html_feedback/issues"
        target="_blank">the following issues</a>. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we
      may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability
      should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
      all.</p>
    <p>Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a <a
        class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/wiki/Porting-LaTeX-packages-for-LaTeXML"
        target="_blank">list of packages that need conversion</a>, and welcome <a class="ltx_ref"
        href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/issues" target="_blank">developer contributions</a>.</p>
  </div>
